item.title: Houston Dash beat Chicago behind Leah Klenke's first goal as a pro
item.description: Leah Klenke (4) and the Dash celebrate her first goal in Friday's win over Chicago. (Daniel Bartel/NWSL via Getty Images) CHICAGO - Leah Klenke scored her first goal as a professional as the Houston Dash beat the Chicago Stars 3-1 on Friday. The Dash have earned seven points in last three road matches under interim coach Jaime Frias. Houston took a 1-0 lead in the fourth on a free kick into the box from Lisa Boattin that was stopped but Klenke got the rebound and scored. It was the fastest goal of the season for the Dash. The Dash added another goal in the 54th minute on an indirect kick from Boattin to the far post, where midfielder Maggie Graham finished with the goal. Forward Clarissa Larisey scored Houston's final goal in the 79th minute on a pass from Kiki Van Zanten. The Dash end the season at home on Nov. 1 against Portland. item.title: Lakers outlast Clippers behind big three
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers C Walker Kessler (14) dunks the basketball during an NBA basketball game against the Los Angeles Clippers, Friday October 23, 2026 in Los Angeles, Calif. LOS ANGELES — The Lakers’ big three delivered again on Friday. This time, Austin Reaves supplied the second-half scoring burst, while Walker Kessler helped create separation with his anchoring. Reaves, Luka Dončić and Kessler combined for 73 points as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Clippers 125-117 before a sellout crowd at Crypto.com Arena, improving to 2-0. Reaves finished with 28 points and nine assists, Dončić added 23 points and Kessler contributed 22 points and six blocks. After combining for 77 points in Wednesday’s season-opening win over Golden State, the trio helped L.A. outlast the Clippers in its first crosstown matchup of the season. Rui Hachimura finished with 16 points and six rebounds in his return to L.A. He shot 5 for 14 from the field, including 3 for 6 from 3-point range, in his return. The biggest push came in the third quarter, when Reaves scored 13 points on 6-of-7 shooting and Kessler recorded two blocks. The Lakers outscored the Clippers 39-26 in the period to turn a halftime tie into a 103-90 lead. “It just felt like Walker was everywhere, in that third and really was a huge spark for us getting us a win,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Reaves had 26 points and six assists through three quarters, making nine of his first 10 shots. His efficiency helped carry the offense after Dončić opened the game shooting 2 for 10. Dončić recovered to make six of his final 11 attempts, while Reaves continued finding opportunities to score and create for teammates. The Lakers extended their advantage to 15 in the fourth quarter before the Clippers trimmed the margin. “It was a great response in the second half from everybody,” Kessler said. “But yeah, man, he’s an extremely talented player.” Getting to that point required the Lakers to slow a Clippers offense that shot 63% from the field in the first quarter. L.A. established its own presence inside early, scoring 12 of its first 16 points in the paint. But the Clippers’ shooting put the Lakers behind before their defensive activity helped change the game. Kessler accounted for three of the Lakers’ four blocks in the second quarter as they erased the deficit. By halftime, L.A. had combined for 11 steals and blocks. Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams contributed at both ends, finishing with 13 and 14 points, respectively. LOS ANGELES — The Lakers’ big three delivered again on Friday. This time, Austin Reaves supplied the second-half scoring burst, while Walker Kessler helped create separation with his anchoring. Reaves, Luka Dončić and Kessler combined for 73 points as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Clippers 125-117 before a sellout crowd at Crypto.com Arena, improving to 2-0. Reaves finished with 28 points and nine assists, Dončić added 23 points and Kessler contributed 22 points and six blocks. The biggest push came in the third quarter, when Reaves scored 13 points on 6-of-7 shooting and Kessler recorded two blocks. The Lakers outscored the Clippers 39-26 in the period to turn a halftime tie into a 103-90 lead. “It just felt like Walker was everywhere, in that third and really was a huge spark for us getting us a win,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Reaves had 26 points and six assists through three quarters, making nine of his first 10 shots. His efficiency helped carry the offense after Dončić opened the game shooting 2 for 10. Dončić recovered to make six of his final 11 attempts, while Reaves continued finding opportunities to score and create for teammates. The Lakers extended their advantage to 15 in the fourth quarter before the Clippers trimmed the margin. “It was a great response in the second half from everybody,” Kessler said. “But yeah, man, he’s an extremely talented player.” Getting to that point required the Lakers to slow a Clippers offense that shot 63% from the field in the first quarter. L.A. established its own presence inside early, scoring 12 of its first 16 points in the paint. But the Clippers’ shooting put the Lakers behind before their defensive activity helped change the game. Kessler accounted for three of the Lakers’ four blocks in the second quarter as they erased the deficit. By halftime, L.A. had combined for 11 steals and blocks. Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams contributed at both ends, finishing with 13 and 14 points, respectively. Redick praised their work against Darius Garland and pointed to Thybulle’s second-half 3-pointers as momentum-changing plays. The defensive effort also received an immediate contribution from Collin Sexton, who collected a steal shortly after checking in for his Lakers debut. “He gets the guys going with just his energy,” Kessler said. “That kind of stuff is contagious.” Still, the Lakers left with an issue Redick had emphasized before tipoff: taking care of the ball. They committed 21 turnovers, and Redick was dissatisfied with their execution against the Clippers’ trapping defense while protecting a double-digit lead. The mistakes gave L.A. another area to address despite its productive offensive night. “We know the turnovers is a problem,” Redick said. “We’ll continue to work at it, continue to get better at it.” For a second consecutive game, however, the Lakers received enough from Dončić, Reaves and Kessler to finish with a win. Friday, their production came with a third-quarter defensive effort that gave the offense room to pull ahead.

item.title: Johnson throttles Reagan in Stone Oak Super Bowl to take control of 28-6A
item.description: Johnson's Braelyn Allen celebrates a touchdown during the first quarter of a District 28-6A football game against Reagan on Friday, October 23, 2026 at Heroes Stadium in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News) In its most important district game of the season, Johnson did more than just put up a win. Johnson stifled Reagan 50-7 in the annual Stone Oak Super Bowl on Friday night at Heroes Stadium. In front of a packed Johnson crowd, the Jaguars led the entire game and earned full control of District 28-6A as the last undefeated team. "It feels good, but that's just our expectation," Johnson sophomore wide receiver Braelyn Allen said. "Beating Reagan is just our first step to what we really want to accomplish, which is going to state." Johnson senior quarterback Elvis Estrada said the Jaguars needed to put up a big win Friday. "We've got bigger aspirations than this game," he said. "But the places we want to be, we've got to put up scores like this." Johnson's Jeremiah Johnson rushes for a touchdown during the first quarter of a District 28-6A football game against Reagan on Friday, October 23, 2026 at Heroes Stadium in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News) The Jaguars jumped to an early lead, and the Rattlers never recovered. Johnson junior running back Jeremiah Johnson scored on a 44-yard rushing touchdown with 9:58 left in the first quarter. Reagan lost the ball on the ensuing kickoff, and Johnson recovered it to set up its offense on Reagan's 15-yard line. Allen scampered into the end zone for a one-play scoring drive. As expected, the four-star recruit was a crucial part in Johnson's rivalry win. Allen hauled in seven receptions for 181 yards and two touchdowns. He also rushed twice for 24 yards and two touchdowns. "I'm taking him all day," Estrada said of Allen. The quarterback threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns on 14-of-25 passing with three rushes for 31 yards. Both offenses hit a lull early in the second quarter, but Johnson extended its lead in the final minutes of the period. Estrada hurled a 55-yard pass to senior wide receiver Logan Staggs to place the Jaguars firmly in Reagan territory. Allen rushed into the end zone on the next play for a 9-yard touchdown with 2:38 left until halftime. Estrada then found Allen for his first passing touchdown of the night 38 seconds before halftime on a 23-yard play. Johnson's Noah Cartwright rushes for a short gain during the third quarter of a District 28-6A football game against Reagan on Friday, October 23, 2026 at Heroes Stadium in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News) "It was a really big group win," Estrada said. "We've definitely matured and leveled up from this game." Reagan did not get on the board until well into the second half. item.title: Marion Star Football Player of Week 10 Poll, vote for your favorite
item.description: The Week 10 high school football games in the Marion area played Oct. 23 have been decided. Which player had the best night? You get to decide. Below are the nominees for the Marion Star Football Player of Week 10 Poll. It will be open through 9 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 27 , and fans are encouraged to vote as often as allowed in the live poll that is embedded into this story at MarionStar.com and its app. More on Elgin football: Elgin makes history in its victory over Hardin Northern Week 10 scoreboard: OHSAA high school football scores, Marion Star's live Week 10 updates Marion Star Football Player of Week 10 Poll nominees Elgin's Archer Johnston ran 23 times for 252 yards, three touchdowns, one 2-point conversion and two receptions for 15 years, plus a fumble recovery on defense in a victory over Hardin Northern that clinched a league championship. Northmor's Jackson Welch caught eight passes for 111 yards and a touchdown and returned a kickoff 79 yards for a TD in a win over Loudonville. North Union's Nickolas Hajjar was 20-for-26 passing for 152 yards and a touchdown, plus ran nine times for 49 yards and a TD in a loss to Graham. Mount Gilead's Tyler Harr ran 15 times for 260 yards and six touchdowns in a win over Cardington-Lincoln. Highland's Kane Stover accounted for 400 all-purpose yards after running 24 times for 245 yards and two touchdowns, passing for 2 of 3 completions for 67 yards and a TD, returning two punts for 88 yards including an 84-yard TD return, plus he produced 15 tackles on defense in a win over Pleasant. Pleasant's Keean Perriguey caught four passes for 130 yards and two touchdowns, plus made an interception on defense in a loss to Highland. Last week's winner Pleasant's Weston Shaffer, who scored three touchdowns in a loss to Shelby, earned 3,866 of 8,154 votes for 48 percent to win the Marion Star Football Player of Week 9 Poll. Marion Harding's Mattic Simmers, who ran for 49 yards on 11 carries and scored a touchdown, plus picked off a pass and made 6.5 tackles on defense in a loss to Galion, had 3,468 votes for 43 percent. Other nominees were Northmor's Brad Bowlin, Elgin's Finn Van Gundy, Ridgedale's Billy Wren, Mount Gilead's Tyler Harr, North Union's Trenor Kyte and Highland's Kane Stover. rmccurdy@usatodayco.com 419-610-0998 X @McMotorsport Instagram @rob_mccurdy_star This article originally appeared on Marion Star: Marion Star Football Player of Week 10 Poll, vote for your favorite

item.title: Medina Valley rushing duo powers Panthers over MacArthur
item.description: Medina Valley running back Kevin Straughter (2) stiff arms a defender during the UIL football game against MacArthur Friday Oct. 23, 2026, Panther Stadium in Castroville, Texas. (Sam Grenadier/Contributor) CASTROVILLE - Kourtney Bratcher and Kevin Straughter combined for 278 yards rushing and four scores Friday as Medina Valley continued its romp through District 14-5A-I with a 63-10 win over MacArthur at Panther Stadium. Both Panther runners rushed for at least 100 yards and two scores as Medina Valley (8-0, 5-0) took one more step towards winning its second straight district title, while MacArthur (4-4, 2-3) lost its third in a row after a 2-0 district start. Bratcher rushed for 173 yards, with one of his two scores an explosive 61-yard touchdown run in third quarter, while Straughter chipped in 105 yards rushing, as they combined for more than half of Medina Valley's 458 yards on the ground. Bratcher said the mindset of Medina Valley's offense is to never let off the pedal. "Stay on the gas, stay locked in and that's pretty much it," Bratcher said. Medina Valley running back Kourtney Bratcher (34) runs through a tackle during the UIL football game against MacArthur Friday Oct. 23, 2026, Panther Stadium in Castroville, Texas. (Sam Grenadier/Contributor) In addition, quarterback Hunter Hurtado, who is the maestro of the Panthers' Flexbone offense, ran for 67 yards and three touchdowns as Medina Valley scored at least 50 points for the seventh time this season and marked the third game this season the Panthers have reached the 60-point plateau. "It's very fun, but it's also a very explosive offense," Straughter said. "I feel like we can all enjoy together the success that we're getting. I feel like you can't predict what we're going to do. We may motion one way, fake the run, pass. I feel like you can't just setup for us, it's kind of like a game time adjustments." Medina Valley coach Andrew Britt said his squad is going to continue to do what it has been doing effectively throughout season - mixing it up on the field. "Honestly, we're just going to stay doing what we do," Britt said. "We're going to run the football and we're going to take some shots. We're going to throw the football. Honestly, we stay the course, never too high, never too low. Just trying to figure it out and take one play at a time." Medina Valley took the opening drive and scored in just five plays, capped off by Straughter's 19-yard touchdown three minutes into a game for a 7-0 lead. MacArthur scored on its opening possession as well, as Afton Royal drilled a 47-yard field goal to cap off a 10-play drive at 4:48 in the first quarter. That would be the closet MacArthur would get, as Medina Valley stepped on the gas in scoring 34 unanswered points, all in the second quarter, to go up 41-10 at halftime. (Sam Grenadier/Contributor) CASTROVILLE - Kourtney Bratcher and Kevin Straughter combined for 278 yards rushing and four scores Friday as Medina Valley continued its romp through District 14-5A-I with a 63-10 win over MacArthur at Panther Stadium. Medina Valley coach Andrew Britt said his squad is going to continue to do what it has been doing effectively throughout season - mixing it up on the field. Honestly, we stay the course, never too high, never too low. Just trying to figure it out and take one play at a time." Medina Valley took the opening drive and scored in just five plays, capped off by Straughter's 19-yard touchdown three minutes into a game for a 7-0 lead. That would be the closet MacArthur would get, as Medina Valley stepped on the gas in scoring 34 unanswered points, all in the second quarter, to go up 41-10 at halftime. Hurtado started the second quarter scoring explosion with a 14-yard touchdown run. A punt block by defensive lineman Rhys Wheeler set up the Panthers' next score, a 5-yard Bratcher run. Straughter followed with a 42-yard scoring run and Hurtado registered his second touchdown on a 22-yard scoring run. Mason Kennedy capped off the big quarter for Medina Valley with a 24-yard scoop and score fumble recovery. MacArthur was able to break through for its only touchdown, a 38-yard scoring pass from Turner Schwartz to Kellen Polansky on the last play of the first half. Members of the Medina Valley football team sing the school song after the UIL football game against MacArthur Friday Oct. 23, 2026, Panther Stadium in Castroville, Texas. "We did a pretty good job (defensively) for the most part," Britt said. "We let one slip away right before the half. That's really frustrating, honestly. You never want to do that in the last four minutes of a half. We let one go and that's on us and we'll get it fixed, and the kids responded. I thought we played great in second half after doing that." Medina Valley hopes to close in on another district crown when it hosts Jay next Friday, while MacArthur, which is still in the playoff picture, hopes to end its three-game slide when it takes on second place Southside Thursday at Heroes Stadium. item.title: NFL Week 7 International Series Best Player Props—Steelers Vs. Saints
item.description: Jaylen Warren has averaged 119.7 scrimmage yards this season. Getty Images The NFL Week 7 International Series contest is in Paris, and it features the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints. The 4-2 Steelers are 3.0-point favorites against the 2-4 Saints, and the game’s total is 44.5 points. The weather forecast calls for enough wind to potentially impact the passing game, namely explosive, downfield passing. The field could also be wet from overnight and pre-game rain. The two forthcoming best player props are a scrimmage yardage over for one of the contest’s running backs and an under for one of the pass-catching options. NFL Week 7: International Series (Paris) Best Player Props Jaylen Warren Over 90.5 Rushing + Receiving Yards (-120) at Fanatics Sportsbook Pat Freiermuth Under 32.5 Receiving Yards (-113) at DraftKings Sportsbook Jaylen Warren (Pittsburgh Steelers - RB) Jaylen Warren is having a fantastic season, amassing 718 scrimmage yards (rushing and receiving yards combined) in six games. He’s averaging 119.7 scrimmage yards per game, with a median of 102. The do-it-all back has cleared 90.5 rushing-plus-receiving yards in three games, including two of his last three. Rico Dowdle returned from a three-game absence last week. Sadly, Warren has gone over 90.5 scrimmage yards in three games without Dowdle and under in three games with Dowdle. Still, Warren’s usage was encouraging last week. Warren had a 73.7% snap share and 14 rush attempts versus Dowdle’s 27.6% and seven. In Week 6 , Warren also had a 38.9% route participation rate compared to Dowdle’s 13.0%. Ultimately, Warren tallied only 78 scrimmage yards. That said, Warren’s matchup was challenging. The Buccaneers held running backs to 59 rushing yards per game, 3.35 yards per carry and 35.6 receiving yards per game before Week 6. Warren has a mouthwatering matchup this week. The Saints have coughed up an NFL-high 116.8 rushing yards per game, 4.83 yards per carry, 30.8 receiving yards per game and 7.32 yards per target to running backs. Jahmyr Gibbs (186 scrimmage yards), Ashton Jeanty (93 scrimmage yards), Bijan Robinson (147 scrimmage yards) and Aaron Jones (117 scrimmage yards) all surpassed Warren’s line of 90.5 scrimmage yards against the Saints this season. Warren could also be without Dowdle or with a diminished Dowdle this week. Dowdle was a limited participant once and a full participant in practice twice last week with a toe injury. He has logged only three limited participations in practice this week with a knee injury and is listed as questionable. item.content:encoded: Jaylen Warren has averaged 119.7 scrimmage yards this season. Getty Images The NFL Week 7 International Series contest is in Paris, and it features the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints. The 4-2 Steelers are 3.0-point favorites against the 2-4 Saints, and the game’s total is 44.5 points. The weather forecast calls for enough wind to potentially impact the passing game, namely explosive, downfield passing. The field could also be wet from overnight and pre-game rain. The two forthcoming best player props are a scrimmage yardage over for one of the contest’s running backs and an under for one of the pass-catching options. NFL Week 7: International Series (Paris) Best Player Props Jaylen Warren Over 90.5 Rushing + Receiving Yards (-120) at Fanatics Sportsbook Pat Freiermuth Under 32.5 Receiving Yards (-113) at DraftKings Sportsbook Jaylen Warren (Pittsburgh Steelers - RB) Jaylen Warren is having a fantastic season, amassing 718 scrimmage yards (rushing and receiving yards combined) in six games. He’s averaging 119.7 scrimmage yards per game, with a median of 102. The do-it-all back has cleared 90.5 rushing-plus-receiving yards in three games, including two of his last three. Rico Dowdle returned from a three-game absence last week. Sadly, Warren has gone over 90.5 scrimmage yards in three games without Dowdle and under in three games with Dowdle. Still, Warren’s usage was encouraging last week. Warren had a 73.7% snap share and 14 rush attempts versus Dowdle’s 27.6% and seven. In Week 6 , Warren also had a 38.9% route participation rate compared to Dowdle’s 13.0%. Ultimately, Warren tallied only 78 scrimmage yards. That said, Warren’s matchup was challenging. The Buccaneers held running backs to 59 rushing yards per game, 3.35 yards per carry and 35.6 receiving yards per game before Week 6. Warren has a mouthwatering matchup this week. The Saints have coughed up an NFL-high 116.8 rushing yards per game, 4.83 yards per carry, 30.8 receiving yards per game and 7.32 yards per target to running backs. Jahmyr Gibbs (186 scrimmage yards), Ashton Jeanty (93 scrimmage yards), Bijan Robinson (147 scrimmage yards) and Aaron Jones (117 scrimmage yards) all surpassed Warren’s line of 90.5 scrimmage yards against the Saints this season. Warren could also be without Dowdle or with a diminished Dowdle this week. Dowdle was a limited participant once and a full participant in practice twice last week with a toe injury. He has logged only three limited participations in practice this week with a knee injury and is listed as questionable. Warren should clear his rushing plus receiving yardage prop with or without Dowdle, but the best time to bet his player prop is now, as the line will climb if Dowdle is ruled out. Pat Freiermuth has struggled against the coverage types deployed the most often by the Saints. Getty Images Pat Freiermuth (Pittsburgh Steelers - TE) Pat Freiermuth has averaged 30 receiving yards per game this year, with a median of 31.5. He’s fallen short of 32.5 receiving yards in four of six games, including last week’s contest. In fact, one of the two times Freiermuth cleared that mark was in Week 1. Thus, he’s gone under in four of five games since. Freiermuth has a favorable matchup through one lens. The Saints have allowed the fifth-most receiving yards per game (75.8) and the eighth-most yards per target (8.58) to tight ends this year. However, that comes with the caveat that the Saints have faced Sam LaPorta, Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer, Kyle Pitts and Isaiah Likely. They’ve faced a murderer’s row of tight ends. Through another lens, the matchup is a stone-cold disaster for Freiermuth. The Saints have played zone coverage at the fourth-highest rate (83.0% versus 73.7% league average) and single-high coverage at the third-highest rate (64.2% compared to 49.8% league average) this season. Their marks aren’t too dissimilar to Tampa Bay’s 81.5% zone rate and 65.1% single-high coverage rate, and the Buccaneers held Freiermuth to a season-low 11 receiving yards last week. Freiermuth’s struggles last week shouldn’t be handwaved away. Instead, they illustrate a continuation of his issues against those coverage types. Freiermuth has logged 0.11 targets per route run (0.19 TPRR league average) and 1.18 yards per route run (1.62 Y/RR league average) on 89 routes against zone and 0.12 TPRR (0.20 TPRR league average) and 0.71 Y/RR (1.58 Y/RR league average) on 101 routes against single-high coverage this year. The Saints should bottle up Freiermuth and hold him under 32.5 receiving yards, making the under on his player prop an alluring bet. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Canada inflict back-to-back losses on England
item.description: WXV Global Series Canada (12) 31 Tries: Omokhuale, De Goede 3, Bauder Cons: De Goede 3 England (7) 22 Tries: Feaunati, Cokayne, Sing Cons: Harrison, Sing Pens: Harrison Head coach John Mitchell said England need a "new stimulus" after losing 31-22 to Canada in the WXV Series in Ottawa to suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade. The hosts ran in five tries to England's three, including a hat-trick for captain Sophie de Goede, as they backed up last weekend's 24-21 win in Toronto, which ended the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten streak, with another statement victory. It completes a 2-0 series win for Canada after the two sides also shared a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September. After losing multiple matches in a calendar year for the first time since 2016, world champions England head into their meeting with the USA in New Jersey next Friday (21:15 GMT) hoping to avoid three consecutive losses for the first time since 2013. England made a promising start, Maddie Feaunati crashing over from close range inside 10 minutes, but Canada hit back twice in quick succession through Julia Omokhuale and De Goede to lead 12-7 at the break. Zoe Harrison kicked a penalty early in the second half before England turned to their driving maul to overturn the deficit, Amy Cokayne walking in their second score. However, De Goede restored her side's lead three minutes later and completed her hat-trick just after the hour-mark before Savannah Bauder danced down the left wing to put Canada out of sight. Emma Sing bagged a consolation try for England in the 80th minute. "Perhaps we have become a little bit predictable," said Mitchell, who arrived in Canada unbeaten as England head coach. "Definitely I'll have to create with the girls the new stimulus in the new year. "Test matches of this quality, the best teams in the world, it always comes down to execution. We presented ourselves many an opportunity and we just didn't quite execute." Lack of TMO a 'turning point' - Mitchell This series has been a landmark occasion for women's rugby, with a record crowd for a standalone women's fixture in North America in attendance in Toronto last weekend for Canada's first home match since August 2025. The Maple Leafs had not beaten England since 2016 and had never done so on home soil. Now, they have done it twice in a row. item.content:encoded: WXV Global Series Canada (12) 31 Tries: Omokhuale, De Goede 3, Bauder Cons: De Goede 3 England (7) 22 Tries: Feaunati, Cokayne, Sing Cons: Harrison, Sing Pens: Harrison Head coach John Mitchell said England need a "new stimulus" after losing 31-22 to Canada in the WXV Series in Ottawa to suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade. The hosts ran in five tries to England's three, including a hat-trick for captain Sophie de Goede, as they backed up last weekend's 24-21 win in Toronto, which ended the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten streak, with another statement victory. It completes a 2-0 series win for Canada after the two sides also shared a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September. After losing multiple matches in a calendar year for the first time since 2016, world champions England head into their meeting with the USA in New Jersey next Friday (21:15 GMT) hoping to avoid three consecutive losses for the first time since 2013. England made a promising start, Maddie Feaunati crashing over from close range inside 10 minutes, but Canada hit back twice in quick succession through Julia Omokhuale and De Goede to lead 12-7 at the break. Zoe Harrison kicked a penalty early in the second half before England turned to their driving maul to overturn the deficit, Amy Cokayne walking in their second score. However, De Goede restored her side's lead three minutes later and completed her hat-trick just after the hour-mark before Savannah Bauder danced down the left wing to put Canada out of sight. Emma Sing bagged a consolation try for England in the 80th minute. "Perhaps we have become a little bit predictable," said Mitchell, who arrived in Canada unbeaten as England head coach. "Definitely I'll have to create with the girls the new stimulus in the new year. "Test matches of this quality, the best teams in the world, it always comes down to execution. We presented ourselves many an opportunity and we just didn't quite execute." Lack of TMO a 'turning point' - Mitchell This series has been a landmark occasion for women's rugby, with a record crowd for a standalone women's fixture in North America in attendance in Toronto last weekend for Canada's first home match since August 2025. The Maple Leafs had not beaten England since 2016 and had never done so on home soil. Now, they have done it twice in a row. But for all the positives, both for Canada and the growth of women's rugby, Mitchell called for "improved standards" around officiating, with connection issues to the television match official (TMO) influencing a "turning point" in the match. Heading into the final 20 minutes, with the match evenly poised 19-17 in Canada's favour, England winger Jess Breach's eyes lit up as she intercepted a pass from Justine Pelletier. The park opened up in front of her for a try which would have moved her into joint-second in the all-time list for England women, but she was pulled back mid-stride for being offside. Moments later, De Goede scored Canada's fourth to put them seven points ahead. "The game potentially needs an improved standard with TMO," said Mitchell. "There was no TMO connection tonight and I think Jess' intercept was probably a turning point that could have influenced the match. "There has been a TMO in the two Test matches but there has been no connection in the stadium. We've definitely got to improve on that. These games are so meaningful and there's going to be situation where they can be major turning points. The girls deserve quality decision-making." De Goede underlines world's best status De Goede got her hands on the Utrecht Shield following Canada's win [Getty Images] In the aftermath of Canada's World Cup final defeat by England last September, De Goede received her women's player of the year gong. Hoisted onto her team-mates' shoulders, she held the trophy aloft, albeit probably not the one she wanted to have her hands on in the moment. She saw off competition from England's Meg Jones and New Zealand's Jorja Miller to become only the second Canadian - man or woman - to win the accolade in 15s. Against England over the past six weeks, she has demonstrated why she is among the best in the world. It was her break down the left wing in Exeter which set up Olivia Apps' game-levelling try. In Ottawa, her versatility was on full display. She charged down the left wing as Senft's support runner for her first try, capitalised on a lapse in concentration from the other 29 players on the park to pick up a loose ball for her second - even having time to raise her arm in celebration, and dotted over for a classic second-row score from a maul to round out her performance. Kicking from her signature red tee - another example of the rising profile of the sport in Canada - she made eight of her 13 conversion attempts across the series. The two she missed in Ottawa were from the left touchline. Line-ups Canada: Bauder; Corrigan, Symonds, Seumanutafa, Hogan-Rochester; Perry, Apps; Nelson, Idowu, Menin, De Goede (c), Royer, Senft, Omokhuale, Gibson. Replacements: Tuttosi, Kassil, Rempel, Forteza, Buisa, Crossley, Pelletier, Tessier. England: Sing; Breach, Jones (c), Rowland, Venner; Harrison, L Packer; Botterman, Cokayne, Bern, Talling, Ives Campion, Burton, Kabeya, Feaunati. Replacements: Field, Carson, Muir, Short, Matthews, Robinson, Aitchison, Kildunne. Officials Referee: Aurelie Groizeleau (Fra) Assistant referees: Luke Rogan (USA) & Amelia Luciano (USA) TMO: Derek Summers (USA)

item.title: Wisconsin volleyball's lapses add up in loss vs. Washington | 3 takeaways
item.description: MADISON – Wisconsin volleyball ’s loss might have been summed up from someone several rows up along one of the sidelines in the UW Field House bleachers right before match point. “We just can’t get out of our own way,” a fan said in an exasperated tone. No. 6 Wisconsin fell to No. 21 Washington in five sets, 25-20, 25-27, 25-21, 18-25, 16-18, on Oct. 23 at the UW Field House. It was the Badgers ’ first loss to a team outside the top 10 of the AVCA coaches poll at the time of the match. The narrow loss for the Badgers had 12 ties and four lead changes in the fifth set alone. (There were 33 ties and 12 lead changes across all five sets.) “And then we make three errors in a row to end it,” Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield said. “And you can’t be doing that.” Mental miscues add up for Badgers in critical moments As Sheffield referenced, Wisconsin did not do itself any favors in the closing stretch. The match ended on a Washington service ace – its eighth of the match. (That was tied for the Badgers’ most reception errors in a match this season.) Before that, UW setter Charlie Fuerbringer picked up her third service error of the match when she served the ball into the net. On the penultimate rally of the match, outside hitter Eva Travis defended a ball that would have gone out of bounds and been a Wisconsin point. That would have given the Badgers a 16-15 lead, and that was before Decelise Champion’s 20th and final kill. Instead, the rally ended with a kill by Washington’s Kylie Kleckner and gave the Huskies the 16-15 lead. Champion’s kill tied it at 16-16 before the Huskies benefited from the Badgers’ service error and reception error. “What you don’t want to do – as that’s coming, your eyes are up, and the line is down, and the people are scrambling – is letting a ball go and it clips the line,” Sheffield said. “You can’t have that happen. So you’d much rather play a ball if you think it’s close in that situation than not.” While those were perhaps the three most recent self-inflicted wounds, they weren’t the only ones in the Badgers’ first home loss of 2026. There was a foot fault call on Jaela Auguste in the set. Sheffield’s group also blew 23-19 and 24-21 leads in the second set. The Huskies finished the set on an 8-2 run and fought off four Wisconsin set points. “You have an opportunity to go up on a team, 2-0, and we let our foot off the gas,” Sheffield said. Wisconsin’s left-side hitters struggle against Huskies A combined 25 kills from Wisconsin’s two starting outside hitters would often be part of a winning formula for the Badgers. It was less effective against the Huskies, however, as Travis and Audrey Flanagan each finished with seven attack errors. Travis hit .083 on 36 swings, and Flanagan hit .211 on 38 swings. Flanagan’s seven attack errors were tied for the second-most in the freshman’s career. It was the Badgers ’ first loss to a team outside the top 10 of the AVCA coaches poll at the time of the match. The narrow loss for the Badgers had 12 ties and four lead changes in the fifth set alone. (There were 33 ties and 12 lead changes across all five sets.) “And then we make three errors in a row to end it,” Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield said. “And you can’t be doing that.” Mental miscues add up for Badgers in critical moments As Sheffield referenced, Wisconsin did not do itself any favors in the closing stretch. The match ended on a Washington service ace – its eighth of the match. (That was tied for the Badgers’ most reception errors in a match this season.) Before that, UW setter Charlie Fuerbringer picked up her third service error of the match when she served the ball into the net. On the penultimate rally of the match, outside hitter Eva Travis defended a ball that would have gone out of bounds and been a Wisconsin point. Instead, the rally ended with a kill by Washington’s Kylie Kleckner and gave the Huskies the 16-15 lead. Champion’s kill tied it at 16-16 before the Huskies benefited from the Badgers’ service error and reception error. “What you don’t want to do – as that’s coming, your eyes are up, and the line is down, and the people are scrambling – is letting a ball go and it clips the line,” Sheffield said. “You can’t have that happen. So you’d much rather play a ball if you think it’s close in that situation than not.” While those were perhaps the three most recent self-inflicted wounds, they weren’t the only ones in the Badgers’ first home loss of 2026. There was a foot fault call on Jaela Auguste in the set. Sheffield’s group also blew 23-19 and 24-21 leads in the second set. The Huskies finished the set on an 8-2 run and fought off four Wisconsin set points. “You have an opportunity to go up on a team, 2-0, and we let our foot off the gas,” Sheffield said. Wisconsin’s left-side hitters struggle against Huskies A combined 25 kills from Wisconsin’s two starting outside hitters would often be part of a winning formula for the Badgers. It was less effective against the Huskies, however, as Travis and Audrey Flanagan each finished with seven attack errors. Travis hit .083 on 36 swings, and Flanagan hit .211 on 38 swings. Flanagan’s seven attack errors were tied for the second-most in the freshman’s career. Travis’ only matches in 2026 with more attack errors were UW’s losses to then-No. 5 Stanford and then-No. 3 Kentucky. (She had 10 and eight errors, respectively, in those matches.) “We were not great from the left pin out of system, and we were having a tough time scoring,” Sheffield said. “Washington was fantastic in that area of the game – out-of-system attacking – and we weren’t. … We’ve got to continue to expand our range. We’ve got to continue to expand our shot-making skills.” Decelise Champion shines, but Washington’s star steals spotlight Wisconsin star freshman Decelise Champion put together another outstanding performance, finishing with 20 kills while hitting .352. It tied her career-high and was the 17-year-old’s eighth match with 11 or more kills. “Decelise was fantastic,” Sheffield said. “Playing with a lot of courage.” Washington’s star pin-hitter was the one who truly captured the spotlight in the match, though. Simona Mateska, a second-year player from Serbia, finished with 31 kills against the Badgers while hitting .424. She finished with the most kills by a Washington player in a single match since 2013 and the third-most kills by a Washington player in the 25-point rally scoring era. It also tied the UW Field House record for kills by an opposing player in the 25-point rally scoring era. Baylor’s Yossiana Pressley also had 31 kills in a four-set match in 2019. “I thought Mateska was clearly just the best player on the court tonight,” Sheffield said while Champion was sitting next to him. “Thirty-one kills, hitting .424 – that’s a monster night. We had a tough time slowing her down. Our block was pretty much nonexistent against her.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Wisconsin volleyball's lapses add up in loss vs. Washington | 3 takeaways

item.title: Cowboys’ Christian Parker gets real on Mike Pettine not attending practices in new role
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Cowboys’ Christian Parker gets real on Mike Pettine not attending practices in new role appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker isn’t concerned about senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine ’s absence from team practices. Instead, Parker believes the veteran coach can contribute to the Cowboys’ defensive preparations without spending every session on the field , following Pettine’s recent arrival in Dallas. Pettine has taken an unconventional approach to his responsibilities, focusing on film study and game-planning rather than attending practices alongside the rest of the coaching staff. According to Jon Machota, the Cowboys believe Pattine’s time is better spent analyzing opponents and helping develop defensice strategies behind the scenes. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When asked about the arrangement, Parker offered a humorous response that suggested he had no concerns about Pettine’s absence. “There’s a lot of people on the practice field that don’t need to be there,” Parker joked The remark highlighted Parker’s willingness to let members of his coaching staff contribute in different ways rather than requiring everyone to follow the same routine. For Pettine, whose coaching background includes experience as an NFL defensive coordinator and head coach, the arrangement allows him to concentrate on preparation and analysis. His responsibilities remain important even without a regular presence on the practice field, particularly when it comes to studying opposing offenses and identifying potential adjustments. Parker’s comments also suggest that Dallas is comfortable dividing coaching responsibilites according to where eachstaff member can provide the most value. The arrangement aligns with Pettine’s previously outlined role as an additional set of eyes on game days. Ultimately, the Cowboys’ defensive coordinator made it clear that Pettine’s absence from practice is not an issue within the coacing staff. Related: Skip Bayless’ shocked reaction to Cowboys being favorites vs. Eagles on MNF Related: Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer addresses offensive concerns with confident self boast

item.title: 'We have to think about posting 350 first': Haris Rauf on need for bigger totals in modern-day cricket
item.description: Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has explained his role alongside Shaheen Shah Afridi and Naseem Shah, saying their main job is to take important wickets and help the team win matches. Speaking to the media in Lahore, Rauf highlighted the importance of teamwork as Pakistan look to continue their strong performance in the ongoing ODI tri-series. “My role, along with Naseem and Shaheen, is to take wickets for the team. This is a team game, and everyone is supporting one another,” Rauf said. He also praised Shaheen’s presence in the bowling attack, saying his inclusion gives Pakistan an added advantage. “Having Shaheen in the team is always beneficial,” he added. Pakistan’s bowling plans and growing run rates Pakistan have started the tri-series well, winning their opening matches against Sri Lanka and England. Rauf said successfully defending a total of 300 runs was encouraging, but teams now need to score more runs because modern-day cricket has become more aggressive. “Defending 300 runs is a good sign. Our effort is to ensure that the bowling unit continues to perform well. When teams are scoring more than 300 or 400 runs, we also have to think about posting totals of 350 and defending them,” he said. Rauf also stressed that taking wickets during the middle overs is important to stop opposition batters from scoring freely and building strong partnerships. “You have to take wickets in the middle overs. Wherever you play in the world, runs are scored because cricket has changed,” he remarked. Rauf focuses on pace as Pakistan prepare for England Rauf believes fast bowlers remain a major weapon in modern cricket. He said he is working on improving his fitness and speed to become more effective for Pakistan, while keeping his attention on performances rather than criticism. “A fast bowler is an X-factor in today’s cricket. I continue to work on my fitness and pace so that I can give people fewer reasons to talk,” he said. The pacer also backed Pakistan batters Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to deliver important contributions in the remaining matches. After beating Sri Lanka and England, Pakistan will return to action against England in the fourth match of the tri-series at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on Sunday, following a two-day break. The team will aim to maintain its winning momentum with strong performances from both its batting and bowling units.

item.title: Jorge Martin declared unfit for Australian GP after suffering fracture in sprint
item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP title contender Jorge Martin will miss Sunday’s Australian Grand Prix after breaking his forearm in a high-speed crash in the sprint. In a statement released less than two hours after the sprint, Aprilia revealed that the Spaniard has suffered a fracture to his radius, one of the two bones in the forearm. Initial scans also indicated a suspected fracture of the ulna, the other forearm bone, at its distal end near the wrist. While further tests are necessary to establish the full extent of the injury, Martin has already been declared unfit for the grand prix on Sunday, dealing a severe blow to his title hopes. “Jorge Martin was taken to the circuit’s medical center following his crash,” the statement read. “The x-rays revealed a fracture of the radius and a suspected fracture of the ulna at the distal end. “Martin will undergo further examinations to reach a definitive assessment of his condition. Martin has been declared unfit for tomorrow’s race.” Later on Friday, Aprilia issued a second statement, revealing that the team will decide how to proceed with the situation based on additional tests. "Martin is set to undergo a CT scan in Melbourne to determine the extent of the injury and whether the ulna is affected," it said. "If the radius fracture is non-displaced, he will remain there in an attempt to race in Sepang; if there is displacement or if the ulna is also fractured, he will travel to Spain as soon as possible for surgery." IT'S OVER FOR MARTINATOR 😔 @88jorgemartin has gone down fast at Turn 8 #AustralianGP 🇦🇺 https://t.co/Uu9ybRkFgZ — MotoGP™🏁 (@MotoGP) October 24, 2026 Martin was in the middle of a thrilling battle with Ducati’s Marc Marquez for victory in Saturday’s half-distance race at Phillip Island when he crashed out of second place on lap 8. Replays showed him sliding into the gravel at 180km/h before being put on a stretcher and taken to the medical centre for check-ups. With Marquez going on to win the race, Martin went from leading the championship by two points to dropping 10 points behind his Ducati rival, a 12-point swing against his favour. Martin had made a brilliant launch from fourth on the grid to move directly behind his title rival, and even passed him for the lead on lap 3. But he made a mistake two laps later and dropped back to second, with the pair continuing to trade positions until Martin crashed with six laps to run. With the Spaniard retiring, team-mate Marco Bezzecchi emerged as Aprilia’s best representative in the race in fourth. Explaining the incident, Martin said: "It’s a shame about this crash. It was a nasty one. But I’m okay, despite a hard, very dangerous impact. "Now I’m going to have some tests done to see exactly what the situation is, and then we’ll decide how to proceed based on the results." item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo MotoGP title contender Jorge Martin will miss Sunday’s Australian Grand Prix after breaking his forearm in a high-speed crash in the sprint. In a statement released less than two hours after the sprint, Aprilia revealed that the Spaniard has suffered a fracture to his radius, one of the two bones in the forearm. Initial scans also indicated a suspected fracture of the ulna, the other forearm bone, at its distal end near the wrist. While further tests are necessary to establish the full extent of the injury, Martin has already been declared unfit for the grand prix on Sunday, dealing a severe blow to his title hopes. “Jorge Martin was taken to the circuit’s medical center following his crash,” the statement read. “The x-rays revealed a fracture of the radius and a suspected fracture of the ulna at the distal end. “Martin will undergo further examinations to reach a definitive assessment of his condition. Martin has been declared unfit for tomorrow’s race.” Later on Friday, Aprilia issued a second statement, revealing that the team will decide how to proceed with the situation based on additional tests. "Martin is set to undergo a CT scan in Melbourne to determine the extent of the injury and whether the ulna is affected," it said. "If the radius fracture is non-displaced, he will remain there in an attempt to race in Sepang; if there is displacement or if the ulna is also fractured, he will travel to Spain as soon as possible for surgery." item.title: Basha rolls over Brophy to keep momentum going
item.description: This is the Basha team everyone envisioned before the season. After starting the season 1-2, with a tough loss to Orange Lutheran (California) and then getting blown out by Phoenix Pinnacle, the hype around the Bears seemed to quiet down. Basha entered the season as the favorite to repeat as Open Division state champions and were ranked No. 11 in the country by USA TODAY. But those two losses appeared to dampen the enthusiasm around the team. Since then, Chandler Basha has rattled off five straight wins and looks every bit like the team that generated so much talk in the offseason. No. 4 Basha (AIA/Max Preps 6A) dominated visiting No. 7 Phoenix Brophy Prep 42-17 on Oct. 23 to improve to 6-2 on the season. “It for sure hurt that we lost those two games early on,” said Basha senior running back Noah Roberts, who had two touchdowns in the win against Brophy. “It humbled us. It really made us hit the reset button and reflect on ourselves. Now, you see we’re picking up steam.” Basha coach Chris McDonald said the early-season losses were a moment for introspection. “The big thing that we talked about was having a mirror moment and it started with me and myself taking accountability for things,” McDonald said. “We're playing a schedule that a lot of teams aren't playing, but really it was all front loaded." He added: “I am proud — and we're not done yet — of how they've handled adversity. Being told the whole offseason how good you're going to be and all this other stuff, then things don't go the way that you expected. And here we are.” Brophy jumped out to a 7-0 lead early in the second after a scoreless opening frame. Then, Basha took over. First it was a 12-yard run from senior quarterback Jake Rodgers to tie it with 8:22 left in the second. After Basha forced two punts, Roberts put his stamp on the game. A 40-yard run from Roberts, a Texas commit, put Basha deep into the red zone. The next play, Roberts punched it from seven yards out to take a 14-7 lead with 2:32 remaining in the second. A quick three-and-out from Brophy’s offense on the ensuing drive gave Basha the chance to score right before halftime and the Bears made quick work of it, going down the field in seven plays in less than a minute – aided by a two Brophy penalties – and extending the lead to 21-7 on a nine-yard touchdown run from Rogers. Brophy added a field goal just before half to cut the lead to 21-10. Basha wasted little time coming out of the half, with Roberts delivering the effective knockout punch on a 70-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage to make it 28-10 with 11:13 left in the third quarter. item.title: Serie A Preview: Udinese vs Milan – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: Serie A Preview: Udinese vs Milan – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Kosta Runjaic’s future at the Bluenergy Stadium could be on the line when his downtrodden Udinese side takes on Serie A giants Milan on Sunday night. Both sides will be desperate to add to their point tally, albeit for different reasons. After a promising start to the season (W1, D1), Udinese’s form has fallen off a cliff. Runjaic’s men have lost five consecutive league matches and are currently tied on points with 18th-placed Fiorentina, while enduring their worst losing streak since 11 defeats in a row back in 2018. Needless to say, Runjaic is walking a tightrope despite keeping Udinese safe from relegation in both previous seasons in charge of the Friulian club. Finding a way out of that stressful losing run has become imperative for the German coach, who oversaw a stunning 3-0 win over Milan at San Siro last season. However, things have dramatically changed for the Rossoneri in the meantime. Ruben Amorim, who replaced Massimiliano Allegri in the summer, has yet to lose a Serie A fixture this season (W4, D3), with Milan entering this round as one of only four teams still unbeaten in Italy’s top flight. Even so, the 19-time Italian champions come out of another underwhelming European night, with Bournemouth thrashing them 3-0 in midweek Europa League action. In Amorim’s defense, he refused to field his best starting XI at the Vitality Stadium, so fresh legs could help Milan return to the win column on Sunday. Match Preview Udinese Udinese’s decline began with back-to-back losses to Milan’s fierce top-four rivals Inter and Lazio in September. While the Friulians could be forgiven for squandering a two-goal lead in a thumping 5-3 defeat at Giuseppe Meazza, a 3-0 home loss to Lecce last weekend was a bitter pill to swallow for perennial mid-table tenants. Yet, Lecce’s win didn’t come as a big surprise, given Udinese’s notorious home struggles. Runjaic’s men have won just one of their last nine league matches at the Bluenergy Stadium (D2, L6), and they can hardly expect to defy that abysmal record here against Milan, at least based on their recent meetings in Udine. The hosts have lost their last three home league matches against the Rossoneri, conceding at least three goals on each occasion. The picture becomes even bleaker when factoring in Udinese’s dreadful run of six successive defeats in Sunday-held Serie A games. Milan Things have gone terribly wrong for Milan in the Europa League, where they’ve lost two of their three matches without scoring (W1). However, the visitors can draw confidence from their decent Serie A start under Amorim, as they bid to open a new top-flight season on an eight-game unbeaten run for just the third time in the last 20 years. On a positive note, Milan have lost only three away league outings since the beginning of last season (W12, D8). Match Preview Udinese Udinese’s decline began with back-to-back losses to Milan’s fierce top-four rivals Inter and Lazio in September. While the Friulians could be forgiven for squandering a two-goal lead in a thumping 5-3 defeat at Giuseppe Meazza, a 3-0 home loss to Lecce last weekend was a bitter pill to swallow for perennial mid-table tenants. Yet, Lecce’s win didn’t come as a big surprise, given Udinese’s notorious home struggles. Runjaic’s men have won just one of their last nine league matches at the Bluenergy Stadium (D2, L6), and they can hardly expect to defy that abysmal record here against Milan, at least based on their recent meetings in Udine. The hosts have lost their last three home league matches against the Rossoneri, conceding at least three goals on each occasion. The picture becomes even bleaker when factoring in Udinese’s dreadful run of six successive defeats in Sunday-held Serie A games. Milan Things have gone terribly wrong for Milan in the Europa League, where they’ve lost two of their three matches without scoring (W1). However, the visitors can draw confidence from their decent Serie A start under Amorim, as they bid to open a new top-flight season on an eight-game unbeaten run for just the third time in the last 20 years. On a positive note, Milan have lost only three away league outings since the beginning of last season (W12, D8). Yet, they have shared the spoils on three consecutive Serie A road trips and could make it four away league draws on the bounce for the first time since 2017. With table-topping Inter already four points away, the Rossoneri will be keen to avoid that unwanted feat here. A bit more urgency from the get-go would help. Still, ten of Milan’s 14 league goals this season came after the hour mark, suggesting patience could be key to unlocking Udinese’s defense. That rings especially true when bringing their zero-goal first-half tally in away league action into the equation. Team News Udinese lost star defender David Alaba to injury in the Austrian’s maiden Serie A start last weekend, with the former Bayern Munich and Real Madrid ace joining Vakoun Bayo and Idrissa Gueye in the treatment room. However, Nicolo Zaniolo finally returns to the fold from injury, though Keinan Davis should lead the line for the home side. Milan’s relatively short injury list features Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, and Samuel Chukwueze, whose absence could prompt Amorim to deploy Diego Moreira as a right wingback. Goncalo Ramos, who didn’t travel to England with the rest of the team on Thursday, should regain his place in attack. Udinese vs Milan Potential Starting Lineups Udinese (3-4-2-1): Okoye; Bertola, Solet, Ebosse; Vojvoda, Karlstrom, Piotrowski, Kamara; Ekkelenkamp, Gomez; Davis. Milan (3-4-2-1): Maignan; Tomori, De Winter, Pavlovic; Moreira, Musah, Modric, Bartesaghi; Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos. Udinese vs Milan Prediction Udinese’s rotten patch puts Milan firmly in the driver’s seat, but the Rossoneri’s knack for dropping points on the road isn’t to be taken lightly. Nevertheless, the visitors can’t ask for a more favorable opportunity to put Thursday’s heartbreak firmly behind them than this one.

item.title: Caitlin Clark’s contract dilemma awaits Indiana Fever after Amber Cox firing
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images The Indiana Fever face a major decision over Caitlin Clark’s future after reportedly parting ways with general manager Amber Cox, leaving the franchise searching for new leadership ahead of a crucial offseason. The Athletic reported that Cox’s departure came just hours after team president Kelly Krauskopf announced she was stepping down, creating two significant vacancies in Indiana’s front office. The next general manager will be tasked with building a championship contender around Clark and Aliyah Boston while also deciding how to approach Kelsey Mitchell’s free agency. Caitlin Clark could earn projected $1.7 million salary with Indiana Fever Clark’s next contract is one of the biggest issues facing Indiana , with the new WNBA collective bargaining agreement potentially allowing the guard to earn a significant increase on her current salary. The Fever star could qualify for a projected maximum salary of $1.3 million in 2027 through the Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract provision, known as EPIC. Clark meets the eligibility criteria after earning first-team All-WNBA honours in 2024. She could then sign an extension beginning at a projected $1.7 million in 2028, subject to the applicable requirements and salary limits. Those figures would represent a substantial rise from the $530,000 she earned in 2026. However, Clark has made it clear that money is not her only priority. Speaking during her exit interview, the Fever star said: “My focus is on winning. I certainly know what I deserve and what I’m worth, but at the same time, sometimes you have to make sacrifices.” Clark has also indicated that she intends to remain in Indiana, giving the franchise some reassurance as it works through its contract plans. Cox joined the Fever in 2024 as chief operating officer and general manager, having previously held executive roles with the Dallas Wings and Connecticut Sun. During her tenure, Indiana failed to progress beyond the WNBA semifinals, with its latest playoff campaign ending in a first-round defeat to the Las Vegas Aces. Krauskopf’s departure adds further uncertainty. She helped establish the Fever in 2000 and oversaw their 2012 championship, making the search for her successor another important task. Mitchell’s unrestricted free agency also demands attention. Keeping her alongside Clark and Boston would preserve Indiana’s core, although expensive deals could limit the team’s ability to strengthen its supporting cast. The Fever are also investing $78 million in a new practice facility scheduled to open in March 2027. Their next leadership group must now turn the attention surrounding Clark into a team capable of competing for a championship. Read more: Stephen A. Smith blames Caitlin Clark fans for sleeping on Angel Reese ‘If they continue…’ – Lara Trump warns WNBA over national anthem snub ‘Keep it going’ – Indiana Fever fans call for complete overhaul after Team President Kelly Krauskopf steps down

item.title: 'They talk too much!' - Man Utd managerial candidates blast 'out of control' dressing room as Michael Carrick nears the sack
item.description: Manchester United FC v Crystal Palace FC - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Manchester United find themselves in a familiar state of turmoil as potential managerial successors express serious reservations about the culture within the first-team squad. With Michael Carrick fighting for his job, those tipped to replace him have reportedly identified a lack of discipline as the club's primary internal hurdle. Dressing room indiscipline alarms suitors Manchester United’s worst start to a campaign in 40 years has left Carrick on the brink of dismissal. With just one victory in seven Premier League matches, the club are exploring alternatives to the coach they appointed in the summer. However, those approached to take over at Old Trafford are reportedly alarmed by the current squad dynamics. The Red Devils recently suffered a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como in Italy. This dismal run has prompted unprecedented public outbursts from senior players, severely damaging the dressing room's reputation among top European coaches. Potential successors have highlighted a severe lack of respect and discipline within the ranks. First-team stars have a history of outlasting permanent managers at Old Trafford, frequently facing accusations of playing major roles in dismissals and downing tools during difficult periods. Outbursts highlight internal chaos FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Over the past fortnight, the fractured nature of the United squad has become public knowledge. Following a defeat to Atletico Madrid, Lisandro Martinez openly criticised technical director Jason Wilcox . The defender claimed Wilcox failed to assemble a squad capable of competing across four competitions. Club captain Bruno Fernandes then targeted Carrick directly. Speaking after Wednesday's heavy loss to Como, the Portuguese midfielder blamed the manager's tactics for a performance where United were continually exposed and ripped apart. These public complaints have not gone unnoticed by potential replacements. According to The Telegraph , a source close to one candidate stated: "It’s clear they need order and discipline. The dressing room is out of control and that is the first thing to fix." Another candidate's confidant shared similar sentiments. They claimed that the players "talk too much" and must show far more respect for a club of United's stature. Carrick fights back as successors circle Despite the mounting pressure, Carrick remains defiant. Speaking ahead of the upcoming Premier League fixture against Bournemouth, the manager reiterated his demand for maximum effort from his squad - echoing the exact message he delivered in the aftermath of the Como disaster. The club hierarchy, however, are actively evaluating heavy-hitting replacements. Although he stepped down from Newcastle United in the summer intending to take a break from the game, the opportunity to manage the massive Manchester outfit could cut his sabbatical short. Immediate pressure and future prospects Carrick Carrick must immediately secure a positive result against Bournemouth to temporarily ease the intense scrutiny on his position. Another domestic setback could force the board's hand before the situation completely unravels. If a change is made, the incoming manager will inherit a deeply flawed squad that requires immediate structural discipline. item.title: Enzo Maresca could unleash a midfield masterstroke as Manchester City face Aston Villa
item.description: Enzo Maresca could unleash a midfield masterstroke as Manchester City face Aston Villa Manchester City take on Aston Villa today at Villa Park. Enzo Maresca’s side enter today’s match sitting top of the Premier League after making a flying start to the 2026-27 season. City have a perfect 21 points out of a possible 21 and have made a strong start to life under their new manager. However, they face a tough test today against Unai Emery’s Aston Villa side. Villa have won five of their past six matches in all competitions and City haven’t won in four matches at Villa Park. Looking at today’s match, the midfield battle looms as the key component of today’s game. Due to this, it could be the first time that Enzo Maresca unleashes Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in midfield in a bid to take control of today’s match. Starting Elliot Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi, and Enzo Fernandez in midfield may be key for Manchester City against Aston Villa. Manchester City know today’s match will be a tough one against Aston Villa. Unai Emery is one of the elite managers in European football. City have a perfect 21 points out of a possible 21 and have made a strong start to life under their new manager. However, they face a tough test today against Unai Emery’s Aston Villa side. Villa have won five of their past six matches in all competitions and City haven’t won in four matches at Villa Park. Looking at today’s match, the midfield battle looms as the key component of today’s game. Due to this, it could be the first time that Enzo Maresca unleashes Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in midfield in a bid to take control of today’s match. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Flyers did not have a great start to the 2026-27 campaign. They lost each of their first nine games of the season. Things have turned around somewhat, though. Philadelphia has won each of its last three games. The Flyers made the Stanley Cup Playoffs last season . They even won a playoff series over their intrastate rival, the Pittsburgh Penguins . Everything that could have gone right last year did. Philadelphia expected more of the same this season. So far, it’s been tough sledding for the Flyers. They are trying to turn things around. The first step was escaping last place in the Metropolitan Division, which they have done. Now, they need to continue stringing together wins. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Flyers, regardless of their position months from now, should be active in the trade market. At this rate, it appears the team would be sellers rather than buyers. This would be unfortunate, considering their ambitions. At the same time, they do have some veteran talent that would attract attention around the NHL. But it was young defenseman Cam York who was recently named a potential trade candidate for the Flyers by The Athletic. “York is a legitimate top-four defenseman in the league and has a team-friendly contract, too, at $5.15 million AAV through 2029-30 without any trade protection. If the Flyers are to take a big swing at a high-end player in the near future, they’re inevitably going to have to part with a current player or two. York would certainly have interest around the league,” Kevin Kurz wrote. With this in mind, here are two potential landing spots for York early in th 2026-27 campaign. item.title: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson gets doubtful designation vs. Arizona State
item.description: INPHO via Imagn Images Kansas State QB Avery Johnson gets doubtful designation vs. Arizona State appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson’s availability for Saturday’s matchup against Arizona State at Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, Arizona, is now in serious doubt. The 21-year-old was initially listed as questionable on Wednesday before retaining that designation over the following two days. The Wildcats subsequently moved him to doubtful on Friday’s availability report, leaving backup Jacob Knuth as a potential starter versus the Sun Devils. Johnson’s injury concerns emerged during Kansas State’s Week 7 win over Kansas. Johnson took a hard fall at the end of a 59-yard run early in the first quarter and remained on the ground for several minutes while receiving attention from the team’s medical staff. He missed only one play before returning to the game and finishing without any obvious limitations. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Johnson later completed 14 of 24 passes for 209 yards and a touchdown while adding 132 rushing yards against the Jayhawks. He also alluded to shoulder soreness during his postgame interview. The senior has started 32 consecutive games for the Wildcats and has accounted for all but six of the team’s 193 pass attempts through six games. He has accumulated 1,763 total yards and 13 touchdowns while completing 63.1% of his passes, with three interceptions. If Johnson cannot play, Knuth could receive his first big opportunity to lead Kansas State’e offense. The fifth-year quarterback has appeared in three games this season versus Nicholls, Washington State and Kansas. This season, Knuth has completed one pass for seven yards and added 25 rushing yards and a touchdown on three carries. The Wildcats could also consider sophomore Dillon Duff, who is listed alongside Knuth as a backup quarterback. Duff has yet to play this season and has appeared on injury reports since Kansas State’s loss to Cincinnati in Week 4. Meanwhile, Blake Barnett has been out since the season opener against Nicholls while recovering from a lower-body injury that has required crutches. The Wildcats could also use Rodney Fields or Joe Jackson for direct snaps in a wildcat formation. Fields scored a four-yard touchdown on the play Johnson missed versus Kansas. Kansas State is slated to release its final availability report approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled 3:45 p.m. ET kickoff. Related: Texas’ AD refuses to hit panic button amid Arch Manning slump Related: Why Nick Saban was blown away by Kalani Sitake, BYU Cougars win over Notre Dame

item.title: Skip Bayless’ shocked reaction to Cowboys being favorites vs. Eagles on MNF
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Skip Bayless’ shocked reaction to Cowboys being favorites vs. Eagles on MNF appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Skip Bayless is famous for his passionate devotion to the Dallas Cowboys , but even he cannot wrap his head around the latest betting lines for Monday Night Football. Speaking on a show with sports commentator Stephen A. Smith, Bayless expressed complete shock after oddsmakers installed Dallas as 4.5-point road favorites against the Philadelphia Eagles . Despite his usual relentless optimism for his favorite franchise, Bayless candidly admitted that he has lost all faith in his squad right now. “We’re like baying at the moon, you know, we don’t have an offense or a defense,” Bayless said. “I don’t know, Stephen A. They’re four and a half point favorites going to Philadelphia… and I don’t know how they’re favorites because the truth is, my gut feeling is Philly will just figure out how to win that game even without Jalen Hurts.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When SKIP BAYLESS, president of the Cowboys fan club, tells me everything I need to know… Don’t miss our full conversation! https://t.co/ae5WUWTY9T pic.twitter.com/roqL5Xr8Y7 — Stephen A Smith (@stephenasmith) October 24, 2026 The concern from Bayless stems from a frustrating start in Big D. The Cowboys enter this high-stakes divisional matchup sitting at a 2-4 record while struggling across all phases. Quarterback Dak Prescott has struggled to carry the offense despite averaging over 270 passing yards per game, throwing 10 touchdowns against five interceptions. Meanwhile, the Dallas defense ranks near the bottom of the NFL in stopping crucial third-down conversions. Conversely, Philadelphia has repeatedly found ways to secure hard-fought victories at home. Even when star quarterback Jalen Hurts sits out with an injury, head coach Nick Sirianni relies on a heavy rushing game and timely defensive takeaways to control game tempo. For a sports media personality who typically defends Dallas through thick and thin, Bayless sounding this defeated says everything about the team’s current state . Oddsmakers in Las Vegas might see a golden opportunity for Dallas to capitalize against a banged-up rival, but Bayless remains convinced that Philadelphia will prevail. If Prescott fails to deliver on the road on Monday night, the hot seat in Texas will get scorching hot for everyone involved. Related: Cowboys’ Christian Parker gets real on Mike Pettine not attending practices in new role Related: Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer addresses offensive concerns with confident self boast

item.title: Why Nick Saban was blown away by Kalani Sitake, BYU Cougars win over Notre Dame
item.description: © Gary Cosby Jr. / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Why Nick Saban was blown away by Kalani Sitake, BYU Cougars win over Notre Dame appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nick Saban has seen just about everything in college football, but BYU’s upset of Notre Dame still left a lasting impression on him. The ESPN College GameDay analyst was in Provo last weekend when the No. 8 Cougars stunned the No. 2 Fighting Irish 28-24 at LaVell Edwards Stadium . Speaking on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Friday, the legendary former Alabama coach said nothing in his time on the show has matched it . “That was the most excitement and energy and passion that I’ve seen, you know, in college football since I’ve been on the show,” Saban said. “Of course, when I was coaching, you never saw that part of the game.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "That was the most excitement and passion that I've seen since I've been on College GameDay.. That BYU team plays with so much confidence and it starts with Coach Sitake" ~ Coach Saban #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/n7HFNjjCh0 — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 23, 2026 Saban, now in his third season on GameDay, pointed to BYU head coach Kalani Sitake as the driving force behind the Cougars’ fearless performance. “The leadership there, the coach, I mean, he’s like dancing before the freaking game,” Saban said. “I see that kind of confidence, and I didn’t see a lot of guys that were tight or had a lot of anxiety the way they went out there and played and competed in the game. I think that’s a reflection of his leadership and the way he goes about coaching his team, and a confidence they have in themselves.” That confidence showed up when it mattered most. Down late, BYU put together a 10-play, 55-yard drive capped by a 6-yard touchdown pass from Bear Bachmeier to tight end Walker Lyons with 1:47 left. The defense then held on as CJ Carr’s final throw sailed past Jaden Greathouse as time expired, sending fans pouring onto the field. Bachmeier was spectacular, throwing for 224 yards and a touchdown , running for two more scores and even hauling in a touchdown catch on a backward pass. He became the first FBS player in 30 years to record a rushing, passing and receiving touchdown against an AP Top 5 opponent in the same game. Notre Dame was the highest-ranked opponent BYU has beaten since No. 1 Miami in 1990. The win also sent the Cougars soaring to No. 2 in the AP Top 25, their highest ranking since their 1984 national championship season. Now 6-0, BYU will try to stay unbeaten when it faces UCF on Saturday. Related: Texas’ AD refuses to hit panic button amid Arch Manning slump Related: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson gets doubtful designation vs. Arizona State

item.title: Warriors will ‘lose sleep’ over late collapse in loss to Grizzlies
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Brandin Podziemski converted a contested layup, the Grizzlies called timeout and the Warriors’ fifth-year guard amped up the crowd as he retreated to his bench. Podziemski put Golden State up 11 with 5:19 to play, and De’Anthony Melton drained a 3 96 seconds later to extend the lead to a dozen with less than 4 minutes left. Then, in the words of Steph Curry, “pretty much everything went wrong.” Curry and the rest of the Warriors were still processing their epic fourth-quarter collapse Friday night as they boarded the bus to take them to the airport. Golden State missed its final nine attempts from the field, allowing the Grizzlies to mount a 17-0 run and treating their fans to a 111-108 loss in their home opener. Stephen Curry stands on the side of the court during the final moments of the Warriors’ 111-108 loss to the Grizzlies at Chase Center on Oct. 23, 2026 in San Francisco. Getty Images Less than 24 hours later, the Warriors will have to do it all again in Phoenix, still in search of their first win. And will likely have to do so without Curry, who said he will “probably not” suit up against the Suns in the second half of the first back-to-back of the season as the Warriors try to manage his workload. That only made the win slipping out of their hands sting all the more. “It’s a tough pill to swallow,” Curry said, “considering we played really solid, especially in that second half, to give ourselves a lead and be in control of the game for as long as we did.” Golden State fell behind by as many as 13 points in the first half as the Warriors struggled to manufacture offense without Curry or to contain Grizzlies rookie Cameron Boozer, who outclassed fellow first-rounder Yaxel Lendeborg in their first NBA matchup. The last of Boozer’s 25 points came on a turnaround over Brandin Podziemski with 20 seconds to play that gave the Grizzlies their first lead since late in the third quarter, 108-106. Draymond Green was called for his third illegal screen of the game, and Ty Jerome was able to drive uncontested for a layup to finish off his 28-point night — as well as the Warriors’ collapse. After their 128-105 loss to the Lakers on opening night , Golden State is 0-2 for the first time since 2020-21. That’s two games with a healthy Curry they won’t get back. “There’s losses, and there’s ways that you lose like tonight that sting a little bit more,” Curry said. “Everybody says there’s another game tomorrow. But the idea of how important every game is for us … and the fact that we gave one away like this, you might lose a little sleep over it.” Stephen Curry is fouled by Scotty Pippen Jr. during the second half of the Warriors’ loss to the Grizzlies. Getty Images A few possessions earlier, Podziemski and Melton collided while going after a loose ball that Podziemski had poked free. It ended up in the hands of a Memphis player.
