The last of Boozer’s 25 points came on a turnaround over Brandin Podziemski with 20 seconds to play that gave the Grizzlies their first lead since late in the third quarter, 108-106. Draymond Green was called for his third illegal screen of the game, and Ty Jerome was able to drive uncontested for a layup to finish off his 28-point night — as well as the Warriors’ collapse. After their 128-105 loss to the Lakers on opening night , Golden State is 0-2 for the first time since 2020-21. That’s two games with a healthy Curry they won’t get back. “There’s losses, and there’s ways that you lose like tonight that sting a little bit more,” Curry said. “Everybody says there’s another game tomorrow. But the idea of how important every game is for us … and the fact that we gave one away like this, you might lose a little sleep over it.” Stephen Curry is fouled by Scotty Pippen Jr. during the second half of the Warriors’ loss to the Grizzlies. Getty Images A few possessions earlier, Podziemski and Melton collided while going after a loose ball that Podziemski had poked free. It ended up in the hands of a Memphis player. It was, as coach Steve Kerr said, one of “like eight different things [that] had to happen.” “I think if any one of those eight doesn’t happen, we win the game. It was just an avalanche.” Kerr was given a technical for arguing Green’s illegal screen on Jerome that gave up the ball on the Warriors’ final possession. Kerr said it was a “shocking” call by the referees. Ty Jerome celebrates in the final moments of Grizzlies’ comeback win over the Warriors. Getty Images “We probably had six illegal screens tonight, and those were really tough because the flopping that was happening on every single one,” Kerr said. “[It] looked like guys were going down like they’ve been hit by a car or something. … “All those illegal screens really hurt us.” Kerr, however, took a more measured stance than Curry. “There’s 80 [more] games. We’ve lost a couple. We’ll bounce back,” he said. “You don’t think, ‘Does this sting more than any other game?’ You just move on.”

item.title: Barcelona legend calls Vinicius’ absence a big loss for Real Madrid ahead of El Clasico – “He’s important”
item.description: Barcelona legend calls Vinicius’ absence a big loss for Real Madrid ahead of El Clasico – “He’s important” With El Clasico just around the corner, big footballing personalities have started giving their predictions for the first showdown of the season. While Gerard Pique expects an easy win for Barcelona, former Real Madrid star Guti believes Jose Mourinho’s men could come out on top . Now, Jordi Alba has chimed in with his own verdict. The former Barcelona left-back, who enjoyed plenty of fierce duels with Real Madrid during his career, backed his old club to prevail while weighing in on the significance of Vinicius Jr’s suspension. Alba on Vinicius’ absence Will Vinicius’ absence come back to haunt Real Madrid? (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Speaking to Diario AS , Alba acknowledged that the suspended Brazilian represents a major loss for Real Madrid, having faced him on numerous occasions himself. “He’s an important player for them. He’ll miss the game, and that’s a significant loss. Real Madrid has a very deep squad to replace him, and whoever comes in will surely do very well ,” he said. The Barcelona legend went on to detail just how dangerous an opponent Vinicius always proved to be. “He’s a very dangerous player in one-on-one situations. Very fast. He always created a lot of danger. In that sense, you didn’t want him facing Barcelona too often because he always had great games. He’ll be a significant loss for them ,” he added. Alba was also candid in admitting the forward’s absence tilts the contest further in Barcelona’s favour. “Obviously. Some people say it’s good for the spectator to see everyone on the field, but I always say that anything less than top-quality players on the opposing team makes it easier to win ,” he said. Alba’s prediction for the Clasico The former defender did not hesitate in predicting an easy win for his former club, citing the form the team has shown this season. Alba is confident Barcelona can win on Sunday. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) “I see the team doing well from afar. I’m certain they can play a good match and win. They’re having a great season so far, and I hope they can continue that way and take all three points ,” he said. Pressed on what he thinks will happen on Sunday, Alba said he expects Barça to dominate the proceedings. “A Clasico is different from any other. It doesn’t matter how the teams are playing. I’m certain Barcelona is playing very well, and I have complete faith that they will continue to do so and win the match. I’ll be happy if Barcelona wins ,” he added. Asked which Real Madrid player worried him most, the Barcelona icon insisted his old side have nothing to fear. “Watching Barcelona gives me a lot of peace of mind. They have some very talented players up front. But seeing how Barça is playing, I’m honestly calm. If they play as they always do, I have no doubt that Barcelona will win the game,” he said. Finally, Alba was also asked about refereeing controversies

item.title: Jordi Alba talks Yamal, Vinicius, Ballon d’Or and score prediction ahead of El Clasico – “I’m predicting a win”

I’m certain they can play a good match and win. They’re having a great season so far, and I hope they can continue that way and take all three points ,” he said. Alba is confident Barcelona will win vs Real Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The former defender expects Barcelona to secure an emphatic victory, unlike Guti, who is hoping for a Real Madrid win . “A Clasico is different from any other. It doesn’t matter how the teams are playing. I’m certain Barcelona is playing very well, and I have complete faith that they will continue to do so and win the match. I’ll be happy if Barcelona wins.” Asked which Real Madrid player worried him most, Alba admitted he is calm as Barcelona have shown top form. “Watching Barcelona gives me a lot of peace of mind. They have some very talented players up front. But seeing how Barça is playing, I’m honestly calm. This is the year with the most doubts. If you ask me, I’d say Leo. He’s also having a great season and a fantastic World Cup. “ There’s talk about Mbappe, Lamine… Obviously, I’d go with Lamine because of everything he’s achieving at just 19 years old. He’s one of those players everyone wants to pay to see play ,” he added. On Mourinho and the Clasico tension With Mourinho back for his second Madrid spell, Alba reflected on his memories of facing the Portuguese. “I faced him several times at Valencia. Those Clasicos were incredibly intense matches, but that’s true of all Clasicos. Mourinho has that kind of character. “ He’s a coach I admire, both in his playing style and his communication style. I don’t know him personally, but I think he’s a fantastic manager who has made all his teams great.” He believes the fire that defines the fixture is a feature, not a flaw. “The tension in Clasicos is always there, and that’s great. It means the game is alive, that it’s a Clasico. There are incredibly talented players, for me the best in the world, both at Barcelona and Real Madrid. “ I’ve experienced it in a spectacular way. They’re experienced differently.” Finally, on the officiating storm hanging over the fixture, Alba kept his distance. “The truth is, I’m pretty out of the loop on this whole thing in Miami. I wouldn’t know what to tell you. “There are always opinions, there are always people who see it differently. I respect all opinions. The umpires do their job to the best of their ability. We shouldn’t doubt them,” he concluded.

item.title: Raul Fernandez ruled out of Australian GP, adding to Phillip Island absences
item.description: Motorsport photo Raul Fernandez has been ruled out of Australian Grand Prix at Phillip Island, adding to a growing list of absentees that will leave the MotoGP grid with just 18 out of 22 riders in Sunday's race. Among those missing will be the two riders from the factory Honda HRC team. Joan Mir did not travel to Australia because of the illness that has kept him sidelined throughout the Asian leg of the season, while Luca Marini’s absence from Saturday and Sunday was confirmed on Saturday morning after a virus limited him to just two laps in Friday’s opening practice session. The biggest blow came during the sprint race, when Jorge Martin, who had led the championship until Saturday, crashed while battling Marc Marquez. The consequences were serious: the Spaniard fractured the radius in his right arm, with a fracture of the distal ulna also suspected. He will now have to return to Spain to assess the full extent of his injuries and determine whether surgery is necessary, at a critical stage of the season. Martin was declared unfit, but he will not be the only Aprilia rider missing from Sunday’s race. His fellow Spaniard Fernandez, who rides for Trackhouse Racing, will also sit out the grand prix. Fernandez had already been dealing with fractures to two fingers sustained on Saturday at the Indonesian Grand Prix, when he crashed following contact with Marco Bezzecchi. Fernandez battled through the pain at Mandalika and had hoped to manage his condition carefully at Phillip Island, but he aggravated his injuries in a crash during Friday’s opening practice session. The Trackhouse rider tried to persevere on Saturday despite increasing pain following the latest crash and the bumps around the demanding Australian circuit. However, he was forced to retire from the sprint early of his own accord. Fernandez will therefore miss Sunday’s full-length race after being declared unfit by MotoGP medical director Dr Angel Charte, as confirmed by the American team. 🫢 @25RaulFernandez has gone down too at Siberia And all eyes are on his already injured fingers 👀 #AustralianGP 🇦🇺 https://t.co/Ub08k3KHq9 — MotoGP™🏁 (@MotoGP) October 23, 2026 It remains to be seen whether the #25 rider will be able to compete in the second round of the upcoming triple-header, next weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix. "After the race, Fernandez went straight to a medical assessment with the MotoGP Medical Director and it was found that while the finger fracture is stable, there is inflammation of the soft tissue around the fracture," the statement read. "He has now been declared unfit to take part in the Grand Prix of Australia, on Sunday and will travel to Malaysia for a further medical assessment, on Thursday, to determine if he is able to ride at Sepang." Read Also: Jorge Martin declared unfit for Australian GP after suffering fracture in sprint No factory Honda bikes in Australian GP as Luca Marini withdraws due to virus To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Smith v Puello world title fight predictions
item.description: WBC light-welterweight champion Dalton Smith (left) has won all 19 pro fights with 14 stoppages [Mark Robinson - Matchroom Sport] Dalton Smith will make the first defence of his WBC light-welterweight title on home soil when he faces former champion Alberto Puello in Sheffield on Saturday. Unbeaten Smith, 29, returns to the ring for the first time since becoming world champion with a stunning knockout of Subriel Matias in New York in January. Dominican Republic fighter Puello, 32, is aiming to become a three-time world champion, having lost his WBC belt to Matias on points last year. Smith will have the backing of his home crowd at the Utilita Arena. Can he keep his dream of fighting at Sheffield Wednesday's Hillsborough stadium alive with another win? Or will the tricky and experienced southpaw Puello, who has lost just once in 26 professional fights, ruin the homecoming? BBC Sport spoke to figures from across the boxing world to get their predictions on who will come out on top. Smith v Puello - all you need to know How world champion Smith can become a mainstream star Chantelle Cameron - two-weight world champion "I think it's going to be a great fight, I think there will be a lot of close rounds, but I'm going for a majority decision win for Smith in a really tough fight." Prediction - Smith Darren Barker - former middleweight world champion "What a brilliant fight this is. It's such a terrific match-up with contrasting styles. You have a slick southpaw in Puello and the tough, rugged, well-schooled Smith. Puello being a southpaw will suit Dalton who throws a fantastic right hand. "This is fine margins - high-level chess. I think Dalton will come through via decision, or perhaps a late stoppage, and he will have produced two back-to-back victories to cement his place in the top 15 pound-for-pound rankings." Prediction - Smith Carl Frampton - former two-weight world champion "I think this will be an interesting fight. Both guys have a similar sort of style. Puello is a boxer-puncher who goes really well to the body. He throws that loopy left hand shot quite well that Dalton will have to be quite careful of. "It will be cagey at the start and I think Puello will fall behind a little bit. Dalton is a better boxer than him and better at his game. Puello will then have to come forward and I think that will suit Dalton. "So I see Dalton winning quite a wide points decision." Puello is a boxer-puncher who goes really well to the body. He throws that loopy left hand shot quite well that Dalton will have to be quite careful of. "It will be cagey at the start and I think Puello will fall behind a little bit. Dalton is a better boxer than him and better at his game. Prediction - Smith Denzel Bentley - WBO middleweight champion "It's a good fight and I think Puello is a good fighter but I'm Team Smith. He boxes well and his style has matured. Puello has fast hands and is good in close but Smith can find a way to beat him. If he knocks him out then it's a big statement, but I'll go for a Smith win on points." Prediction - Smith Barry Jones - former super-featherweight world champion "This is a harder fight for Smith than Matias. Matias was a monster, while Puello is a clever boxer who sits on the back foot and punches nice and long. He's southpaw which makes it awkward to adjust your feet and stance. "Ultimately, I think the angles of attack will be the difference for Smith. I think it might be a bit of a frustrating night for him but I think he comes out on top on points. "It will be relatively entertaining - not as exciting as the win over Matias, perhaps - but a good homecoming for the champion." Prediction - Smith Viddal Riley - European cruiserweight world champion "I'm backing Dalton, he's been my guy since we were 12 years old. He was my roomate at every tournament and now is his time as WBC world champion." Prediction - Smith Lee Selby - former featherweight world champion "I'm backing Dalton Smith to beat Alberto Puello and retain his world title. Smith's power, accuracy and impressive stoppage win over Subriel Matias make him a dangerous opponent. "Although Puello's experience and awkward southpaw style could make it a tough fight, I think Smith's power and work-rate will prove too much. Smith to win by unanimous decision." Prediction - Smith Paulie Malignaggi - former two-weight world champion "Puello can be awkward and disrupt rhythm as he did in wins over guys like now WBA champion Gary Antuanne Russell, but Dalton's a big light-welterweight and his boxing is on point as well as intelligent decision-making. "His stoppage win over Subriel Matias was impressive but I see Dalton winning this one on points. Puello will complicate things in some moments, but Smith wins a comfortable decision." Prediction - Smith Ade Oladipo - DAZN presenter "It's a big fight. I think the Utilita Arena - pound-for-pound - is the noisiest venue in the country. To use a football analogy, I think it will have to be a 12th man for Dalton. "I think he's up against it. Puello is a very special talent, as is Dalton who put on a performance of a lifetime in January. "Dalton has a lot of the advantages but Puello comes here with experience at the highest level at this division. He wants the belt back, which he thinks was robbed from him in his loss to Matias. "I do edge towards the current champion because of home advantage, but I wouldn't be shocked if Puello walks away with the belt." Prediction - Smith Adam Smith - DAZN commentator "Dalton is a real hero in Sheffield but Puello is very dangerous. He's a southpaw and a former two-time world champion. "It's a very tough first defence but Dalton has home advantage, the age and the unbeaten record. He probably has plans A, B, C and D. He's a very clever boxer whose background has been perfect - an excellent amateur and a solid professional." "I expect him to come through a very tough test." Prediction - Smith Zelfa Barrett - British lightweight "I think Dalton will stop him late on - round nine or 10. Dalton is just too good for Puello, he'll try to put pressure on but Dalton will just have his number." Prediction - Smith Richie Woodhall - former super-middleweight world champion "Dalton will have a little bit too much speed and a little bit too much flair. The one thing that Dalton has to watch out for is he cannot afford to slow it down to Puello's pace. He's decent with his jab, he likes his opponent to stand in front, he doesn't like it when they move. "If Dalton is in and out with his feet, plays it tricky, he'll be able to beat him fairly comfortably as long as he doesn't stand and trade." item.title: Liverpool already have a star better than Michael Olise and Lamine Yamal
item.description: Liverpool already have a star better than Michael Olise and Lamine Yamal For some time now Rio Ngumoha has been one of the most promising talents in English football. Even before he had kicked a ball for Liverpool's first-team, the teenager was causing problems for senior defenders in training and has now become a fully-fledged member of the England squad at just 18. The youngster's importance to the team has increased under Andoni Iraola, and a recent masterful display against Villarreal in the Champions League showed just how good the talented winger has become. The Champions League has been a stage for Rio to shine on this season, and he is even bettering the likes of Michael Olise and Lamine Yamal in some important metrics. Rio Ngumoha is better than Olise and Yamal After becoming the first player since Kylian Mbappe in 2020 to record two assists, two big chances created, three chances created and complete seven successful take ons in the Champions League, Ngumoha now leads some of the world's best footballers in an important metric. In the Champions League this season, Ngumoha averages 7.4 successful dribbles per 90 minutes, the most in the competition among players to have played over 150 minutes. Olise has averaged 5.0 and Yamal only 4.0. Liverpool have a true wonderkid on their hands with Rio, his ceiling is ridiculously high, but he is already an elite talent capable of going toe to toe with some of Europe's best. The Reds spent £123 million on Bradley Barcola in the summer, and Rio looks every bit as good as the Frenchman. Liverpool won't be planning to sell anytime soon, but it isn't farfetched to assume it would take a similar fee to secure the England international's services. A new deal is in the works for the teenager, and an increasingly important role in Iraola's squad looks guarunteed. Ngumoha can be one of the best in the world for sure, and his dribbling stats prove that he's already not that far off.

item.title: New Mexico’s Jason Eck Makes Head-Turning Comment on NDSU
item.description: New Mexico coach Jason Eck knows well how tough NDSU will be on Saturday. Getty New Mexico head coach Jason Eck understands well the challenge that North Dakota State will bring to Albuquerque on Saturday from his FCS days, but it’s even more than that. Eck regards NDSU as a tougher opponent than the Lobos’ biggest-name opponent, Oklahoma, this season. The Lobos fell short of the upset against the Sooners, 14-6 on Sept. 19. “Really, when you look at everything, how they play in all three phases,” Eck told reporters on Monday, “[NDSU is] probably the best team we’ve played all year when you include everything. Oklahoma, I think, had more freak athletes. But as far as a team and how they play together and how it fits, this is a really, really good football team.” Oklahoma has a 3-3 record in the SEC, and the Sooners have a notable win over former No. 1 Texas in an otherwise roller coaster season. If the Bison outperform the Sooners in beating the Lobos, that could go a long way for the College Football Playoff committee. Eck, who coached against the Bison on South Dakota State ‘s staff in the 2010s, is set on preventing that from happening. His Lobos squad has a slim lead for the Mountain West Conference standings, and a loss will end slim CFP hopes for either the Lobos or Bison on Saturday. More Coaches Than Jason Eck Have Past Beef With Bison New Mexico has a couple of coaches on staff besides Eck, who have previous rivalry encounters with the Bison. Lobos defensive coordinator Spence Nowinsky played against the Bison with Division II Minnesota State-Mankato in the 1990s. Offensive coordinator Luke Schleusner played for North Dakota in the old Bison-Fighting Sioux rivalry, and tight ends coach Zach Lujan played and coached for SDSU against the Bison. “They don’t love North Dakota State,” Lobos linebacker Mercury Swaim told the Albuquerque Journal’s Sean Reider on Tuesday. “They don’t love those guys very much. They definitely (made) that known to us.” New Mexico may not have been indoctrinated into Bison lore as if they’re an old North Central Conference or Missouri Valley Football Conference team, but the bulletin board material is there. Reider detailed more of the Lobos coaches’ stories of playing the Bison, which can be read here . Bison Coach Tim Polasek Addresses Jason Eck’s Ticket Sales Push Eck has been bullish on filling his team’s stadium with Lobos fans on Saturday, especially considering how Bison fans travel. That said, Bison head coach Tim Polasek has his squad ready for the challenge. After all, NDSU hasn’t backed down from any challenge in the transition from FCS titan with 10 national championships to FBS newcomer this year. “Jason’s got some real energy behind this football team, and he’s doing everything in his power to sell tickets. item.title: George Russell reveals truth behind Horner's Red Bull approach
item.description: George Russell has played down Christian Horner 's revelation that Red Bull approached his management over a potential move to the team in 2025, insisting that he never seriously considered leaving Mercedes and suggesting the discussions were simply part of the ongoing rivalry between Horner and Toto Wolff. In his newly released memoir Drive, the former Red Bull team principal revealed that he contacted Russell's representatives during last year's British Grand Prix at Silverstone, at a time when Mercedes were openly pursuing Max Verstappen. Horner explained that he grew frustrated with Wolff's continued interest in Verstappen and decided to respond by exploring the possibility of signing Russell, whose future at Mercedes remained uncertain at the time. "Having grown tired of Toto's challenging approach, I decided to fight fire with fire and approached George Russell's management for a meeting," Horner wrote in his memoir. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures "George was coming to the end of his contract, and if it was OK for Toto to constantly talk about my drivers, then I saw no harm in talking to his about a potential move to Red Bull." Horner also questioned why Mercedes had not yet secured Russell's future despite his strong performances, suggesting that Wolff was waiting for Verstappen to make a decision before committing to the British driver. The discussions took place shortly before Horner's departure from Red Bull in July 2025, with Russell eventually remaining at Mercedes. Russell dismisses Horner's Red Bull approach as tactical Speaking to beIN SPORTS Asia ahead of the United States Grand Prix in Austin, Russell was asked whether he knew about the discussions between Horner and his management and how seriously a potential move to Red Bull was considered. "Not serious at all, to be honest," the Mercedes driver replied. When asked whether Horner's approach was simply a distraction tactic, Russell made clear that he never intended to leave Mercedes, pointing instead to the long-standing rivalry between the two team bosses. "Well, I had zero intention of being anywhere but Mercedes and, of course, between Toto and (with) Christian, there's always a pot being stirred and trying to wind the other up. So, yeah, it was all, I guess, tactical."

item.title: 'It is not good enough' - Morgan Gibbs-White admits Nottingham Forest must fix wasteful finishing after frustrating Ipswich Town draw
item.description: Ipswich Town v Nottingham Forest FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Nottingham Forest playmaker Morgan Gibbs-White has urged his team-mates to be more clinical in front of goal after seeing another Premier League win slip away at Portman Road. Despite dominating Friday night's clash against Ipswich Town, the visitors had to settle for a 1-1 draw after squandering a host of clear-cut chances. Midfielder laments missed Suffolk chances Gibbs-White believes victories will soon arrive for Oliver Glasner's side if they cure the goalscoring woes that cost them two points in Suffolk. Neco Williams cushioned home Daniel Munoz's 13th-minute cross for his first goal since April, before Nikola Milenkovic's short 41st-minute backpass let Julio Enciso slot his maiden Ipswich strike past Matz Sels. Ending a three-game losing run lifted the visitors above Coventry City and Tottenham into 16th . Goal-line clearances deny dominant visitors The Tricky Trees generated 2.31 expected goals from 17 attempts on Friday, taking their league tally to 137 shots - second only to Manchester United's 138 - despite netting a joint-low six goals and dropping seven points from winning positions, just one shy of last term's entire total of eight. Returning playmaker Gibbs-White saw an effort stopped by Christian Walton's toe and cleared off the line by Leif Davis, who also hooked away Dan Ndoye's strike. Speaking to Sky Sports about his team's profligacy in the final third, Gibbs-White said: "This is a question we have been asking ourselves in training. We have been doing shooting drills and if you had seen how they were going in yesterday, it was top. But they just were not in the game. It is a topic of discussion and it is not good enough but I am proud of the boys for keeping going and performing high. "It is a massive mentality and this is a bad phase that we are going through but we need to stay positive, keep the togetherness and mentality and performances. If we keep performing like this, surely we will have to win. The second-half, we were completely dominant and we should have won the game in my eyes. As long as we keep performing like this surely we have to win." Controversial refereeing decision sparks debate Controversy erupted in the 48th minute when Issa Diop felled James McAtee as the midfielder broke through. After initially waving play on, referee Thomas Bramall checked the pitchside monitor for a potential red card before booking the defender, explaining that McAtee "had knocked the ball to the right side of the goal". Speaking to Sky Sports , Glasner insisted it was a "clear red card", though he "liked" the official reviewing the screen and following the "right procedure". Testing fixtures precede international break Although Friday's point nudged Forest out of the drop zone on six points, weekend results elsewhere could immediately plunge them back into the bottom three as they chase just a second league win under Glasner. The East Midlands outfit travel to Brentford next weekend looking to finally convert their high shot volume into goals. They then host Manchester City on November 7 before the upcoming international break.

item.title: Right on time, Reese St. Clair plays hero vs. Claymont football
item.description: This story will be updated. UHRICHSVILLE – For Buddy White, there was no doubt in his mind. Nor was there any in that of his counterpart, Matt Lancaster. If given the chance, Claymont was going for the win. And that’s precisely what White, the Mustangs’ head coach, did with an Inter-Valley Conference-South Division title and unbeaten regular season on the line. When Jackson Jinks caught a 9-yard touchdown pass with 1:11 left in their Week 10 showdown, cutting visiting Indian Valley’s lead to a point, White called timeout to set up strategy for the potential game-winner. He elected for a power run with sturdy Dre’Vonn Searcy to the right, but an unblocked Reese St. Clair made a beeline for the goal line from the secondary. Searcy put his head down, but St. Clair stacked him up just short of the goal-line. The Braves recovered the on-side kick a few seconds later and ran out the clock to secure a hard-earned 7-6 win that looked very little like the majority of their wins in the past four regular seasons. More: Dover football stuns New Philadelphia on last-second TD to win OCC title More: Ohio high school football scores, Tuscarawas-area results from Week 10 More: OHSAA high school football scores, Muskingum-area live updates from Week 10 More: Philo tops Maysville, shares MVL title as Lincicome ties record White didn’t regret the decision – or the play call. “I wanted to win now,” White said of going for the lead, rather than kick the game-tying extra point and hope for overtime. “We had the opportunity to win the game right there. I didn't want to go into overtime and risk somebody getting hurt when we have the playoffs next week." Though big-play man Kamden Stout carried much of the rushing load, with Searcy’s need at his linebacker spot paramount against the Ryker Williams-led Braves offense, it was Searcy who got the call for the two-pointer. A power play from a tight formation, with the back-side guard pulling, right tackle blocking down and fullback leading Searcy into the hole, was a play the team had spent ample time practicing. White said he was at peace with it, adding “I had the right guy running the ball.” "We liked the play and have had success with it,” White said. “Some people down there were telling me he got in, but the officials said he didn't, so I've got to go with what the officials said.” St. Clair said afterward that he wanted to redeem himself for some earlier miscues. The coaches had a simple message during a timeout prior to the conversion attempt. “Somebody had to make a play,” St. Clair said. “All 11 of us. If given the chance, Claymont was going for the win. And that’s precisely what White, the Mustangs’ head coach, did with an Inter-Valley Conference-South Division title and unbeaten regular season on the line. When Jackson Jinks caught a 9-yard touchdown pass with 1:11 left in their Week 10 showdown, cutting visiting Indian Valley’s lead to a point, White called timeout to set up strategy for the potential game-winner. He elected for a power run with sturdy Dre’Vonn Searcy to the right, but an unblocked Reese St. Clair made a beeline for the goal line from the secondary. Searcy put his head down, but St. Clair stacked him up just short of the goal-line. The Braves recovered the on-side kick a few seconds later and ran out the clock to secure a hard-earned 7-6 win that looked very little like the majority of their wins in the past four regular seasons. More: Dover football stuns New Philadelphia on last-second TD to win OCC title More: Ohio high school football scores, Tuscarawas-area results from Week 10 More: OHSAA high school football scores, Muskingum-area live updates from Week 10 More: Philo tops Maysville, shares MVL title as Lincicome ties record White didn’t regret the decision – or the play call. “I wanted to win now,” White said of going for the lead, rather than kick the game-tying extra point and hope for overtime. “We had the opportunity to win the game right there. I didn't want to go into overtime and risk somebody getting hurt when we have the playoffs next week." Though big-play man Kamden Stout carried much of the rushing load, with Searcy’s need at his linebacker spot paramount against the Ryker Williams-led Braves offense, it was Searcy who got the call for the two-pointer. A power play from a tight formation, with the back-side guard pulling, right tackle blocking down and fullback leading Searcy into the hole, was a play the team had spent ample time practicing. White said he was at peace with it, adding “I had the right guy running the ball.” "We liked the play and have had success with it,” White said. “Some people down there were telling me he got in, but the officials said he didn't, so I've got to go with what the officials said.” St. Clair said afterward that he wanted to redeem himself for some earlier miscues. The coaches had a simple message during a timeout prior to the conversion attempt. “Somebody had to make a play,” St. Clair said. “All 11 of us. We just had to make it happen.” Lancaster, Indian Valley's head coach, agreed with White's decision, and not because it happened to work in his team's favor. "I definitely would have gone for two," Lancaster said. "They’re the underdog in that game. They’ve got nothing to lose. They’re already in the playoffs, so I definitely would have gone for it.” Defenses reigned supreme In this down-and-dirty, knuckles-in-the-mud scrap between two longtime rivals, separated by just a few miles on U.S. 36, it was only fitting that the conclusion of this old-school clash ultimately came down to stopping a short-yardage run. It was the first time Indian Valley has been held to less than 21 points since a 35-14 loss to Garaway on Sept. 13, 2023 — a span of 44 games. The 33-game regular-season win streak, however, remains alive and well. “This was a great high school football game between two good teams,” Lancaster said. “Claymont has gotten so much better, and their kids played tough. I think they played the entire first half on our side of the field, but our kids were really resilient tonight and just kept fighting back.” Williams’ 9-yard touchdown run on a keeper and Colt James’ ensuing extra-point, which capped an 11-play, 82-yard drive to start the second half and ate up half of the third quarter, proved to be just enough offense for the Braves. Their usual big-play ability, with the 1,000-yard rusher Williams hurting teams with his arms and legs, was harnessed by Camden McCall and the rest of the Mustangs' hardscrabble front seven. They were also hampered by a bad snap that foiled a potential scoring chance early in the fourth and twice had big plays called back on their next possession due to holding calls. Those led to a third-down sack, as a slippery Williams offered his best Fran Tarkenton impersonation, only to be corralled for an 11-yard loss. It forced a punt from deep in their own territory with 6:10 still showing, which Claymont methodically turned into a potential game-winning 10-play scoring drive. St. Clair had other ideas. "Our kids just kept responding, battling back every time and answering the bell," Lancaster said. "It's relief after any win. That's the feeling you have. But its definitely good for our community and our kids. That was a big-game, playoff atmosphere and that's what both communities deserve." The Braves were the ninth opponent that failed to score more than 10 points against the Mustang defense. It's the primary reason why White is gearing up for a long November. "We're getting ready to go into the playoffs now, and those top teams in our region better watch out for us," White said. "Our kids are on a mission to win playoff games. We want to win multiple games." sblackbu@usatodayco.com; X: @SamBlackburnTR This article originally appeared on The Times-Reporter: Right on time, Reese St. Clair plays hero vs. Claymont football

item.title: Insider: Tug-of-war at Carrington as Two top Man Utd officials argue on Nagelsmann & Howe
item.description: Insider: Tug-of-war at Carrington as Two top Man Utd officials argue on Nagelsmann & Howe Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe have emerged as the two main candidates for the Manchester United job, but the management has yet to reach an internal agreement on either manager. The Premier League giants have been enduring a miserable start to the season under Michael Carrick. The team has only registered two wins in 11 matches across all competitions. The woeful 1-4 defeat to Como in the Champions League could have been the final nail in Carrick’s managerial stint, but the 45-year-old will be in charge when Man Utd host Bournemouth on Sunday. However, some observers believe it is only a matter of time before the Wallsend native is shown the door, as the club is already searching for a replacement. Man Utd directors disagree on Carrick’s replacement (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) In recent days, several sources have identified Howe and Nagelsmann as the favourites for the role, with Antonio Conte relegated to a third choice. Both managers are currently unattached, having left Newcastle and Germany in the summer, and they’re both appreciated by the management, albeit by different directors. According to Carrington insider Sully , Man Utd’s Head of Recruitment Christopher Vivell has been pushing for Nagelsmann since June, as he was against confirming Carrick in a permanent role. Vivell had previously worked with his German compatriot during their time together at RB Leipzig. However, Nagelsmann wasn’t available in June, as he was still at the helm of the German national team. The source reveals that Vivell is once again vouching for Nagelsmann, whereas Man Utd’s Director of Football, Jason Wilcox, prefers a Premier League-proven manager like Howe. Why Howe might have the upper hand over Nagelsmann (Photo by Alex Davidson/Getty Images) As Sully explains, Wilcox might be Howe’s main supporter at Man Utd, but he’s not the only one, suggesting other officials are beginning to rally around the 48-year-old Englishman. Moreover, Wilcox holds a higher position in the hierarchy than Vivell, so unless the latter can convince Sir Jim Ratcliffe or CEO Omar Berrada to back Nagelsmann, the German head coach is unlikely to be appointed. In the meantime, Carrick will be hoping for a swift reaction from his team on Sunday, but will it be enough to save his job? Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.description: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I 2026 live scorecard, toss winner, winning probability, result and highlights from Christchurch originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY MATCH DETAILS: (New Zealand vs. India 2nd T20I) Venue: Hagley Oval, Christchurch Captains: Mitchell Santner ( New Zealand ), Shreyas Iyer ( India ) Toss result: India have won the toss and have opted to field Live Telecast: Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV (India), Sky Sport (New Zealand) Umpires and match officials: Kim Cotton and Shaun Haig (on-field umpires), Cory Black (TV umpire), Chris Brown (reserve umpire), and Ranjan Madugalle (match referee) Match result: TBD Player of the Match: TBD FOLLOW LIVE: Ball-by-ball updates of the match New Zealand vs. India 2nd T20I live match scorecard Follow along with the latest live scorecard here as the match unfolds, or click here for key text commentary updates from the action. New Zealand vs. India 2ndT20I Live Score & Updates Welcome to CricketNews.com's live coverage of the second T20I between New Zealand and India at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. Toss result: India have won the toss and have opted to field Pre-match: Four wickets, two balls and 225 runs were the margin that separated the sides in Christchurch on Thursday, and it was enough to leave New Zealand wondering what else they could have done. The second T20I, at Hagley Oval on Saturday, October 24, will show whether the hosts can turn that frustration into a result or whether India will tighten their grip on the five-match series. Much of the talk before the toss concerns a team-sheet change that India did not plan. Ishan Kishan has pulled out with a groin strain, and that is expected to bring Vaibhav Sooryavanshi back into the side after a long spell on the bench. His numbers are modest in volume but loud in impact, with an average of 30.75 and a strike rate of 186.36 from eight T20Is, so New Zealand will have to decide quickly how to bowl at him. The visitors’ bowlers, however, are the ones with homework to do. Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Axar Patel went for 49 and 51 respectively in the opener, and the home batters took 67 off the last 30 balls, even without Jasprit Bumrah in the opposition attack. Glenn Phillips and Finn Allen already know the surface well, and they will back themselves to hit just as freely again. The weather is unlikely to interfere, with clear skies and no rain forecast, though a sharp evening chill and dew could make the ball slippery late in each innings. Whoever wins the toss will probably choose to chase, and the pitch should reward bold strokeplay once the new ball loses its edge. item.title: Marc Marquez: Jorge Martin was faster but overriding in Australian GP sprint
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez has admitted that Jorge Martin had the pace advantage in the Australian Grand Prix sprint, but he recognised that his title rival was “overriding” as their battle for victory intensified at Phillip Island. The two MotoGP championship contenders engaged in their fiercest battle of 2026 at Phillip Island on Saturday, with Martin repeatedly challenging Marquez for the lead before crashing out on lap eight and handing victory to his Ducati rival. At the start, Martin shot from fourth to second and passed Marquez for the lead on at least three occasions, but ran wide each time and dropped back to second. The 2024 champion launched multiple attacks on Marquez on the decisive lap eight, but the latter managed to repass to his advanvces to assert his position. Their battle came to a premature end at Turn 8 on the same lap when Martin slid into the gravel at high-speed from second, allowing Marquez to cruise to the chequered flag and take a 10-point lead in the championship. Marquez admitted that Martin was quicker than him at Phillip Island, but he knew he could beat him once he realised his countryman was pushing beyond his limits in the race. “[It was a] mental game. You can go in if you have the speed. And, honestly speaking, today he was a bit faster than me. “But in the lap he did right in front of me, I understood two things, and then I saw that it was possible to fight for the victory. “I understood that he was fast but taking a lot of risks. Because he was shaking a lot and overriding a bit. “So at that point, I understood that, ok, it's time to take the risk. “It's true that with13 laps on that level, it's very difficult for both of us to finish the race. But he made the mistake. "I was close to making a mistake. But races are like this.” THIS IS CLASSIC #MotoGP 🎞️ INCREDIBLE BATTLE 🤯 #AustralianGP 🇦🇺 https://t.co/YKgFWs6YTl — MotoGP™🏁 (@MotoGP) October 24, 2026 Aprilia appeared to have a clear advantage over its rivals following Practice on Friday, but overnight showers brought Ducati back into contention, with Marquez claiming a surprise pole on Saturday morning. Ducati ultimately locked out the podium positions in the sprint, with Marco Bezzecchi ending up as the top Aprilia rider in fourth. The Noale-based marque suffered a big blow two hours after the race, when x-ray scans revealed that Martin had suffered a fracture to his forearm, ruling him out of Sunday’s race. Speaking before Martin’s injury was disclosed, Marquez said he had to go on the attack in the sprint, knowing there was a lot more at stake than the three-point difference between first and second. “Title fight,” the nine-time world champion declared. “It was a very tight and difficult battle. item.title: Braves predicted to sign $75M veteran ex-Yankees 3-time All-Star, AL wins leader this season
item.description: Braves predicted to sign $75M veteran ex-Yankees 3-time All-Star, AL wins leader this season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves ' biggest problem has undoubtedly been their starting rotation over the last few seasons, as the group hasn't been able to consistently stay healthy. This season was no different for Atlanta, and it caused problems throughout the year. The pitching staff performed well in the playoffs, but the Braves could have done more to address their needs. When the team failed to acquire a strong No. 2 starter at the trade deadline, Hammer Territory's Scott Coleman felt Atlanta wouldn't have enough. “What is most concerning is there's no one coming to help, other than maybe Robert Suarez. This is the team. It's why Alex not adding more at the deadline was so frustrating. They don't have enough to overcome downturns from the stars," Coleman wrote. The rotation could face major injury concerns next season, as Hurston Waldrep and Spencer Schwellenbach could miss the majority of the year. Outside of Chris Sale, the rotation remains wide open heading into 2027. “While it wasn’t their downfall in the end, the starting rotation has been a constant thorn in the Atlanta Braves’ side for multiple seasons now. For 2026, it was no different. As the page turns to 2027, it’s to see how it shakes up. There will be at least one guarantee. Chris Sale is the ace. You probably guarantee that Bryce Elder is in the mix, too, along with Grant Holmes. After that, we’ll see what happens,” SI’s Harrison Smajovitts wrote. With the Braves needing a top-of-the-rotation starter, Sports Talk ATL's Chase Irle believes Atlanta should sign Sonny Gray. “This is probably the 50th time I’ve written about the Braves potentially acquiring Sonny Gray, whether via free agency or trade. They always seem to have interest, but it has yet to come to fruition. Maybe that changes this offseason. Gray is expected to decline his $30 million mutual option with the Red Sox after another stellar campaign, one in which he recorded a league-leading 18 wins with a 2.72 ERA. That kind of production is going to cost a pretty penny, but Gray seems to find success everywhere he goes,” Irle wrote. Gray tied Christopher Sanchez for the most wins among starting pitchers in the league this season. He would be an excellent addition to Atlanta's rotation, bringing consistency and experience to a group that has struggled to stay healthy. Gray is on a $75 million contract with the Boston Red Sox. Signing him would bolster the Braves' roster in several ways. Atlanta needs to address its rotation this offseason, and pursuing Gray would be a great place to start. item.title: Fans get first look at more Arizona softball newcomers in fall games against Phoenix College, Pima
item.description: Arizona softball team and administrators with the family and former players of the late Larry Ray | Photo courtesy of Arizona Athletics Most of Arizona softball’s players had seen action in the first three fall games, including three players from last year’s squad who are trying to get eligible for fifth seasons. There were still two important newcomers who didn’t see the field in the Red-Blue scrimmage or last week’s doubleheader against UTEP. Freshman pitcher Lilly Hauser and senior transfer Madison Conley finally made their Wildcat debuts in a doubleheader against Phoenix College and Pima Community College. Both made big impacts. The Wildcats won both games. They defeated Phoenix in five innings by the score of 13-0. They returned a half-hour later to defeat Pima College by the score of 10-0. Arizona honored late coach Larry Ray between the two games as family, players, former head coach Mike Candrea , and Arizona athletic director Desireé Reed-Francois gathered on the field. Reed-Francois and Candrea presented the family with a framed memorial. The man credited with popularizing the slap hit was critical to the glory years of the program. Ray served two stints as Candrea’s assistant, including taking over the program when Candrea was absent to coach Team USA in 2004 and 2008. He was with the Wildcats as they won five championships (1991, 1993, 1994, 2006, 2007). He passed away in June. The appearances of the young arm and the big bat weren’t the only firsts of the fall. The Wildcats also got their first home runs of the practice season with three different players hitting one out. The first came from Conley, who was the designated player in both games. The blast came in Conley’s first public at-bat as a Wildcat. The North Texas transfer stepped into the box against Phoenix College with two outs and no one on in the bottom of the first inning. She worked a 3-1 count then launched one towards left-center that was clearly out as soon as it left the bat. It was Arizona’s only run in the first but it was a big one. Arizona’s second and third home runs came in the second game against Pima. Kez Lucas sent a towering shot out to left in the bottom of the first to give Arizona a 2-0 advantage. Liberty transfer JaMaya Byrum had an almost identical homer to the same spot an inning later. The games were played under a modified format where five runs by Arizona ended the inning whether there were three outs or not. The game against Phoenix used the five-inning run rule but the game against Pima went a full seven innings. Arizona also used two designated players in the second game. Both Conley and catcher Elizabeth Moffit took at-bats, giving the Wildcats ten hitters. Hauser started her Wildcat career not in the circle but in the batter’s box. The legacy Wildcat, whose mother Wendy Hauser (née Allen) transferred to Arizona from Ohio State for the 2003 season, showed that she wanted to follow in her mother’s footsteps as a two-way player. There were still two important newcomers who didn’t see the field in the Red-Blue scrimmage or last week’s doubleheader against UTEP. Freshman pitcher Lilly Hauser and senior transfer Madison Conley finally made their Wildcat debuts in a doubleheader against Phoenix College and Pima Community College. Both made big impacts. The Wildcats won both games. They defeated Phoenix in five innings by the score of 13-0. They returned a half-hour later to defeat Pima College by the score of 10-0. Arizona honored late coach Larry Ray between the two games as family, players, former head coach Mike Candrea , and Arizona athletic director Desireé Reed-Francois gathered on the field. Reed-Francois and Candrea presented the family with a framed memorial. The man credited with popularizing the slap hit was critical to the glory years of the program. Ray served two stints as Candrea’s assistant, including taking over the program when Candrea was absent to coach Team USA in 2004 and 2008. He was with the Wildcats as they won five championships (1991, 1993, 1994, 2006, 2007). He passed away in June. The appearances of the young arm and the big bat weren’t the only firsts of the fall. The Wildcats also got their first home runs of the practice season with three different players hitting one out. The first came from Conley, who was the designated player in both games. The blast came in Conley’s first public at-bat as a Wildcat. The North Texas transfer stepped into the box against Phoenix College with two outs and no one on in the bottom of the first inning. She worked a 3-1 count then launched one towards left-center that was clearly out as soon as it left the bat. It was Arizona’s only run in the first but it was a big one. Arizona’s second and third home runs came in the second game against Pima. Kez Lucas sent a towering shot out to left in the bottom of the first to give Arizona a 2-0 advantage. Liberty transfer JaMaya Byrum had an almost identical homer to the same spot an inning later. The games were played under a modified format where five runs by Arizona ended the inning whether there were three outs or not. The game against Phoenix used the five-inning run rule but the game against Pima went a full seven innings. Arizona also used two designated players in the second game. Both Conley and catcher Elizabeth Moffit took at-bats, giving the Wildcats ten hitters. Hauser started her Wildcat career not in the circle but in the batter’s box. The legacy Wildcat, whose mother Wendy Hauser (née Allen) transferred to Arizona from Ohio State for the 2003 season, showed that she wanted to follow in her mother’s footsteps as a two-way player. The elder Hauser was the 2002 Big Ten Player of the Year when she had a 1.00 ERA and hit .393 for the Buckeyes. Lilly Hauaser stepped into the box as a pinch hitter in the bottom of the fourth against Phoenix. She sent a double into right field on the first pitch, knocking in a runner from second. That runner was a pinch runner who took over for Conley. The DP showed her strength by flipping a low, outside pitch into right-center for a two RBI double just ahead of Hauser’s at-bat. Conley went 2-2 with a walk and three RBI against Phoenix in the first game. She was 0-3 in the second game. Lucas had her second straight strong weekend at the plate. She was 1-3 against Phoenix College. She finished 1-3 with 2 RBI and a HR against Pima. The sophomore also got her first innings behind the plate after spending most of the fall at third base and shortstop. Lucas played first base last year, but this year she is listed as an catcher/infielder. Part of that is because Arizona was left with a hole at the backstop position after former Wildcat Emma Kavanagh transferred in the offseason. Moffit transferred in, but there was officially no backup for her until the change to Lucas’ roster position and the addition of Utah State transfer Jaelyn Castillo . Arizona could also add two more catchers to the mix if Sydney Stewart and Grace Jenkins get a fifth year. Arizona used four pitchers, including Hauser. Jenae Berry got the start in the first game. She threw three innings, allowing two hits and two walks. She struck out seven. Sophomore Rylie Holder relieved Berry for the final two innings of the opening game. She allowed a single to the first hitter she faced but it was the only hit against her. She had two strikeouts, three groundouts, and one flyout. Her defense also committed an error behind her. Senior Ryley Harrison started the second game. She went four innings without giving up a hit. The only baserunner got on via a hit-by-pitch. Harrison struck out seven. Hauser went into the circle against Pima to start the top of the fifth. It took the rookie a few batters to settle in, but she eventually got her bearings. The first batter of Hauser’s college career got a single. The young hurler seemed to have exactly the ball she wanted in the next at-bat. The hitter sent it back to the circle, and Hauser knew she wanted to start the double play at second. She just got a bit anxious. Hauser turned with plenty of time to throw but it was high. Arizona was properly backing up the play so it didn’t get away but the overthrow allowed both runners to reach safely. Hauser buckled down. She struck out the next two batters then got a groundout to end things. She seemed to learn from her mistake. She started the sixth with a walk but she got the same ball back to the circle from the next batter. This time the throw to second was true and it went on to first for the double play. Hauser went three innings despite Arizona being ahead 10-0 after four. She surrendered two singles and a walk. She struck out two and got the rest of her outs on the ground. That included an extra out in the top of the seventh when she pitched to four batters despite getting the first three out. Arizona will play three games next week, including taking on their second Division I opponent of the fall. The Wildcats start on Friday, Oct. 30 with a doubleheader against NAIA squads from Park University Gilbert and Benedictine Mesa. They host GCU the following day.

item.title: Mike Brown Reacts to Knicks’ Disappointing Loss to Celtics
item.description: Mike Brown Knicks Celtics Getty New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown shared his reaction as his team lost a disappointing game on the road against the Boston Celtics. The Knicks lost 107-103 to Boston on Friday night at TD Garden, dropping their record this season to 0-2 after a 106-100 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers in their season opener. For a Knicks team that came into the season on a high after winning the 2025-26 NBA Championship, this has not been the start to the season that Knicks fans want to see, nor the team’s head coach, Brown, who was not happy with his team’s effort against the Celtics. Mike Brown Reacts After Knicks Lose to Boston Speaking to reporters after New York lost to Boston on Friday, Brown shared his reaction to the defeat. “It was a physical ball game, and we have to give Boston credit. They had the advantage with the physicality,” Brown said. Mike Brown: "It was a physical ball game, and we have to give Boston credit. They had the advantage with the physicality." He said he thought Boston screened really well. — James L. Edwards III (@JLEdwardsIII) October 24, 2026 Brown said that he was not thrilled that his players decided to complain so much to the referees instead of playing through the physical play of the rival Celtics. Brown said there was a stretch where his team was "bitching" to the refs instead of playing through the physicality. — James L. Edwards III (@JLEdwardsIII) October 24, 2026 The Knicks’ head coach also praised Boston superstar Jayson Tatum , who had 36 points in the Celtics’ victory. “Jayson Tatum did what Jayson Tatum does,” Brown said about Boston’s star. Knicks coach Mike Brown: "Jayson Tatum did what Jayson Tatum does." — Chris Mason (@ByChrisMason) October 24, 2026 Mike Brown Critical of Mikail Bridges One player who really struggled in the game was Mikail Bridges , who scored 0 points in 22 minutes on 0-of-8 shooting. It was a terrible performance by Bridges, whom Brown knows needs to be much better if the Knicks are going to make another title run this season after he was such a key cog in the team’s championship run last year. “He had 3 or 4 wide open 3s, and obviously we want him to make half of them if they’re open, but he’s gotta keep shooting and hopefully they’ll go in sooner than later,” Brown said. Mike Brown on Mikal Bridges' early shooting struggles: "He had 3 or 4 wide open 3s, and obviously we want him to make half of them if they're open, but he's gotta keep shooting and hopefully they'll go in sooner than later." #Knicks — Kristian Winfield (@Krisplashed) October 24, 2026 The Knicks return to the court on Sunday night when they take on the Orlando Magic at home in a game that they will be favored to win, and one that they need to win to avoid going down 0-3 to start the season. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Mike Brown Reacts to Knicks’ Disappointing Loss to Celtics appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo sets new all-time Miami Heat record despite losing first two games
item.description: Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo has had a mixed start to the season with the Miami Heat. The Greek superstar would’ve dreamt of big things when he made his high-profile move from the Milwaukee Bucks in July. However, Miami are now 0-2 from their first two games, with their latest defeat coming against the Detroit Pistons. Despite that, Antetokounmpo has made Heat history. Giannis Antetokounmpo sets new Miami Heat record Antetokounmpo is one of the best players in the NBA. When the Miami Heat managed to snap him up during the off-season, everyone stood up and took notice. It was a massive statement. That move raised the expectation levels, and to be fair to Antetokounmpo, he has delivered in his first two games for his new team. In the Miami Heat’s entire history in the NBA, no player had ever managed to score 30+ points in their first two games – Antetokounmpo has just become the first one to do it: 35 points vs Minnesota Timberwolves 36 points vs Detroit Pistons Unfortunately for him, the Heat ended up losing both games, thus making him just the second player in the franchise’s history to score 35+ points in back-to-back fixtures and lose both. The only other player to do so was Dwyane Wade in 2007. Up next for Antetokounmpo and the Heat is a game against the Charlotte Hornets at the Spectrum Centre. It remains to be seen if they can finally get their first win of the season there. item.title: Manchester United Have a Bigger Problem Than Poor Results
item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - SEPTEMBER 13: Michael Carrick, Manager of Manchester United, during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford on September 13, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Getty Manchester United have spent years trying to convince supporters that the club is moving in the right direction. But the problem isn’t just the poor results themselves. Public disagreements and backlash from former players has made the club’s rebuild look a lot worse than it already does. At some point, fans stop listening to what a club says and start judging it by what happens on the pitch. That is where the challenge facing Manchester United goes beyond football. Euan Jones, Digital PR Specialist at Casinos.com , believes the club’s struggles highlight how quickly a powerful brand can lose control of its own narrative. “Manchester United shows how quickly a powerful brand can find itself fighting to control its own narrative. When poor results are accompanied by public disagreements and criticism from former players, the story becomes bigger than football. Rebuilding trust requires consistency between what an organisation says and what people see it doing.” Jones makes a fair point. Manchester United’s problem isn’t simply that the team has struggled to win consistently. It’s that supporters have heard promises of progress before, and another change of direction won’t mean much unless the club can demonstrate that something has genuinely changed. Manchester United Needs Fans to Believe in the Rebuild Rebuilding a football club requires more than signing prospects and yapping about a long-term vision. The club also needs supporters to believe that the people running it understand what went wrong and have a credible plan to fix it. That trust is difficult to recover when every disappointing result brings another round of questions about recruitment, coaching, and leadership. Criticism from former players only adds to the noise, particularly when it reinforces doubts already circulating among supporters. For Manchester United, the challenge is getting fans to buy into the rebuild itself. That means explaining what the club is trying to build, showing why its decisions fit that plan and accepting that meaningful progress may take time. But patience isn’t unconditional. Supporters can live with setbacks if they see evidence that the club is learning from them. What they won’t tolerate indefinitely is being asked to trust a process that produces the same problems season after season. Jones acknowledges how difficult that task has become, arguing that it will take a lot for Michael Carrick and the squad to rebuild belief and trust. Some supporters may even wonder whether the club has already squandered too many opportunities to win back their confidence. Man U Must Make Its Football Match Its Promises Ultimately, no amount of public relations whitewashing can rescue Manchester Unite

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Getty Manchester United have spent years trying to convince supporters that the club is moving in the right direction. But the problem isn’t just the poor results themselves. Public disagreements and backlash from former players has made the club’s rebuild look a lot worse than it already does. At some point, fans stop listening to what a club says and start judging it by what happens on the pitch. That is where the challenge facing Manchester United goes beyond football. Euan Jones, Digital PR Specialist at Casinos.com , believes the club’s struggles highlight how quickly a powerful brand can lose control of its own narrative. “Manchester United shows how quickly a powerful brand can find itself fighting to control its own narrative. When poor results are accompanied by public disagreements and criticism from former players, the story becomes bigger than football. Rebuilding trust requires consistency between what an organisation says and what people see it doing.” Jones makes a fair point. Manchester United’s problem isn’t simply that the team has struggled to win consistently. It’s that supporters have heard promises of progress before, and another change of direction won’t mean much unless the club can demonstrate that something has genuinely changed. Manchester United Needs Fans to Believe in the Rebuild Rebuilding a football club requires more than signing prospects and yapping about a long-term vision. The club also needs supporters to believe that the people running it understand what went wrong and have a credible plan to fix it. That trust is difficult to recover when every disappointing result brings another round of questions about recruitment, coaching, and leadership. Criticism from former players only adds to the noise, particularly when it reinforces doubts already circulating among supporters. For Manchester United, the challenge is getting fans to buy into the rebuild itself. That means explaining what the club is trying to build, showing why its decisions fit that plan and accepting that meaningful progress may take time. But patience isn’t unconditional. Supporters can live with setbacks if they see evidence that the club is learning from them. What they won’t tolerate indefinitely is being asked to trust a process that produces the same problems season after season. Jones acknowledges how difficult that task has become, arguing that it will take a lot for Michael Carrick and the squad to rebuild belief and trust. Some supporters may even wonder whether the club has already squandered too many opportunities to win back their confidence. Man U Must Make Its Football Match Its Promises Ultimately, no amount of public relations whitewashing can rescue Manchester United if the product on the pitch doesn’t deliver on the promises. The club needs to build a squad capable of competing consistently, recruit players who fit a coherent tactical approach, and give its manager enough stability to implement that vision. Just as importantly, the people making those decisions must be held accountable when things go wrong. Of course, a clear long-term vision doesn’t mean that Manchester United needs to sweep every major trophy this season or next. It just means that there needs to be tangible proof that progress is happening. That’s something that fans can grasp and point towards as a positive sign. Manchester United remains one of the biggest names in the sport. Its history and global following haven’t vanished because of poor results. As Jones suggests, rebuilding trust requires repeated evidence of change. Manchester United’s next chapter will be defined less by what the club promises than by whether it finally delivers. item.title: 3 Takeaways as Amen Thompson scales Mount Wembanyama
item.description: Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson (1) blocks a shot by San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) to secure a 114-110 victory during an NBA game at the Moody Center in Austin, Texas, Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) AUSTIN - The 7-foot-4 Victor Wembanyama was a few feet from the basket when he took the pass from De'Aaron Fox, nothing between him and the game-tying basket but a defender nine inches shorter. The Houston Rockets were going to need a miracle to avoid overtime Friday. Amen Thompson proved the answer to their prayers. The 6-foot-7 forward, who seemed dead to rights against Wembanyama in the post, instead blocked the All-Star center's shot attempt with 0.6 seconds remaining, preserving the Rockets' 114-110 victory at the Moody Center. "That's a freakish athletic play," Spurs guard Dylan Harper said. "I mean, that's one out of a million times that I think anyone's going to do that." Alperen Sengun scored 29 points, Thompson added a 20-point, 10-rebound double-double to his game-saving defensive heroics and Kevin Durant pumped in another 20 points in his old stomping grounds on the University of Texas campus as the Rockets improved to 2-0. The Spurs, last year's Western Conference champions, dropped to 0-2. In that, they can commiserate with the NBA champion New York Knicks, who have also started the season 0-2. Did Wemby overthink tonight? And had he ever had a shot that close to the rim blocked before? No and no. https://t.co/qVkXVqwBaL - Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation) October 24, 2026 Wembanyama scored 25 points to go with 13 rebounds and a pair of blocks, but could not convert in the final seconds with his team trailing 112-110. "Right when he caught it, it was going to be automatic two points," Harper said. "But that's the game of basketball." Asked after the game if he wished he had done anything differently on the last play, Wembanyama answered quickly. "Yes," he said. "I would have dunked the ball." MORE SPURS: Why are the Spurs in Austin this weekend? Thank F1 All five members of the Spurs' starting five ended in double figures, with De'Aaron Fox chipping in 19 points and a game-high nine assists. But the Spurs could not find an answer down the stretch down Sengun, and Thompson's game-sealing block sent them home empty-handed. It was an improvement from the Spurs' 116-102 loss to Oklahoma City that opened the season Tuesday, but did not put a tally in the win column. "We're getting used to playing with each other again and used to playing good teams again," Wembanyama said. The Spurs get their next chance at their first win of the season Saturday, when they travel to Dallas to face a Mavericks team that could be without star forward Cooper Flagg, who injured his shoulder Friday against Indiana. "That's a freakish athletic play," Spurs guard Dylan Harper said. "I mean, that's one out of a million times that I think anyone's going to do that." Alperen Sengun scored 29 points, Thompson added a 20-point, 10-rebound double-double to his game-saving defensive heroics and Kevin Durant pumped in another 20 points in his old stomping grounds on the University of Texas campus as the Rockets improved to 2-0. The Spurs, last year's Western Conference champions, dropped to 0-2. In that, they can commiserate with the NBA champion New York Knicks, who have also started the season 0-2. Did Wemby overthink tonight? And had he ever had a shot that close to the rim blocked before? No and no. https://t.co/qVkXVqwBaL - Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation) October 24, 2026 Wembanyama scored 25 points to go with 13 rebounds and a pair of blocks, but could not convert in the final seconds with his team trailing 112-110. "Right when he caught it, it was going to be automatic two points," Harper said. "But that's the game of basketball." Thank F1 All five members of the Spurs' starting five ended in double figures, with De'Aaron Fox chipping in 19 points and a game-high nine assists. But the Spurs could not find an answer down the stretch down Sengun, and Thompson's game-sealing block sent them home empty-handed. The Spurs get their next chance at their first win of the season Saturday, when they travel to Dallas to face a Mavericks team that could be without star forward Cooper Flagg, who injured his shoulder Friday against Indiana. Here are three takeaways from Friday's loss, which dropped the Spurs to 5-4 all-time in games played in Austin: San Antonio Spurs guard Devin Vassell (24) reacts after nearly saving the ball from going out of bounds during the fourth quarter against the Houston Rockets at the Moody Center in Austin, Texas, Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. The Rockets won 114-110. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Wemby bounced back at least For Wembanyama, Friday marked a bounce-back from a miserable opening night in which he went a career-worst 1-of-13 from the field. The All-Star center turned in his second consecutive double-double, and added two blocks to boot. Before the game, Durant talked about what the next step might look like for Wembanyama on the offensive end. "I just think everybody's next step as a player is to become more efficient, make more shots, less movements, just make the game easier for you," Durant said. "I think that's everybody's next step, not just his. I think that's the goal that we're all trying to reach as players is just to make the game easier for ourselves." Wembanyama's 9-of-21 finish Friday was not quite the paragon of offensive efficiency. It was, however, a marked improvement from his opening-night clang-a-thon against Oklahoma City. Mitch Johnson said he saw Wemby looking around for a pass and that's why he called the final timeout (that negated the 3 pointer) https://t.co/HBE32MDALn - Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation) October 24, 2026 2. Sengun was a beast, though Even with the NBA's reigning Defensive Player of the Year on the roster, the Spurs had little answer for Sengun. The 6-foot-11, 255-pound Turkish bruiser used every ounce of strength to bully the Spurs for baskets in the second half. Sengun scored 14 of his points in the fourth quarter, including one stretch in which he had 11 of the Rockets' 13. "He walked the game down and made some really big plays," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. Sengun went to work in a manner that would have made Shaquille O'Neal proud, using his big body to carve out space in the paint against even the Spurs' most formidable defenders. His biggest basket came with 5:01 remaining, after a pair of Harper free throws had given the Spurs a 97-96 lead. Sengun responded by taking the 7-foot-1 Luke Kornet down under the rim, finishing a tough bucket and drawing a foul. The ensuing free throw put Houston ahead 99-97. The Spurs never led again. 3. Free throws were the difference Unlike in the opener, when the Spurs were undone from the 3-point line, this time the damage came closer to the basket. The Rockets got to the foul line 31 times, making 28. The Spurs had similar volume, with 25 free-throw attempts, but made only 18. On a night when a whole lot else was equal between the two clubs, the Rockets' 10-point edge from the foul line proved decisive. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...
